  "content": "# Auxilio Calendar Visitor — Chrome Extension (Build Plan)\n\n## Context\n\nWe want a **desktop Chrome surface** for registering office visitors directly inside Google Calendar — the richer counterpart to the `auxilio-workspace` add-on. The add-on is mobile-capable but lives under the CardService \"card ceiling\" (no free-form UI, a server round-trip per interaction, fragile form state). An extension escapes that ceiling: full React UI, realtime in-page reactions, smooth state — the better UX the vision calls for (realtime guest updates, per-guest invite toggle, template preview/select, inline edits, an intentional auto-nudge).\n\nStrategy (locked in `Planning-docs/2026-06-18_calendar_visitor_chrome_extension_decision.md`): **one signal — the magic address — many reactors.** The extension is the desktop reactor; the add-on stays the mobile reactor; the engine remains the OAuth holder + dedup/issuance brain. The extension reuses the engine's **existing** `/api/visitor/calendar/addon/*` contract with **zero engine code changes** — only one env line (add the extension's OAuth client ID to the audience allow-list).\n\nDecisions confirmed with the user:\n- **Build tooling: WXT** (batteries-included MV3 over Vite; React 19 + TS).\n- **Event data: Calendar read scope.** Extension holds `identity + calendar.events.readonly`; fetches the canonical event by `eid` via the Calendar API for authoritative `iCalUID` + attendees. DOM is used **only for triggers** (detect open, magic address, live edits), never as data-of-record. Internal-first → no OAuth verification yet, no CASA (Calendar-only).\n\n## Repo & stack\n\n- **New independent repo:** sibling folder `auxilio-extension/` with its own `git init` (mirrors how `auxilio-workspace/` is a self-contained sibling). Own `CLAUDE.md`, own remotes later. **Not** Bifrost, **not** EAS.\n- **Stack:** WXT + React 19 + TypeScript + Vite (under WXT) + `lucide-react`. **Server state: TanStack Query** (matches visitor-web/ops-dashboard; gives optimistic toggles + background refetch for free). **UI/session/event-context state:** a small Zustand store (tiny, not a UI framework). **No MUI/Tailwind/paper** — our own MD3 tokens + thin component wrappers (per root CLAUDE.md design stance).\n\n## Architecture — four MV3 surfaces\n\n```\ncontent script (calendar.google.com)        side panel (the app)\n  • detect event open (URL eid + DOM)         • React + TanStack Query UI\n  • detect magic address (via API fetch)      • roster, toggles, edits,\n  • inject dismissible banner (Option A)        template select, email preview, send\n  • inject \"Register visitor\" button          • talks to background for token + event ctx\n  • read live edits (MutationObserver)                  ▲\n            │  runtime msg / port                       │ runtime msg / port\n            ▼                                            │\n        ┌──────────────────── background service worker ─────────────────┐\n        │ • OAuth: mint+cache Google id_token (engine) + access_token (Cal)│\n        │ • Calendar API client (events.get by eid → iCalUID, attendees)  │\n        │ • engine API client (/addon/draft|patch|preview|send|cancel)    │\n        │ • per-tab \"active event context\" store                          │\n        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                   │ HTTPS (Bearer id_token)\n                                   ▼\n                    office-ops-engine  /api/visitor/calendar/addon/*\n```\n\n**Why this split:** background owns secrets/tokens and all network (one place to verify, thin adapter per umbrella rule). Content script is a dumb trigger/observer. Side panel is pure presentation + server-state.\n\n## Auth model\n\n- `chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow` against Google, **Web OAuth client**, redirect `https://<ext-id>.chromiumapp.org/`, implicit flow `response_type=token id_token`, scopes `openid email profile https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly`.\n  - **`id_token`** → sent as `Authorization: Bearer` to the engine (`verifyAddonIdToken` already verifies audience + `email_verified` + domain gate — `office-ops-engine/src/mastra/modules/visitor/addon-auth.ts`).\n  - **`access_token`** → Calendar API `events.get` for canonical `iCalUID` + attendees.\n- Cache tokens in `chrome.storage.session`; silent re-mint with `prompt=none` on expiry (~1h).\n- **Engine change (the only one): add the extension's OAuth client ID to `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`** (comma-list, already supported per spec §3) in `env.updated`. No code change.\n\n## Engine integration — reuse, don't rebuild\n\nAll endpoints already exist in `office-ops-engine/src/mastra/modules/visitor/routes.ts` (ID-token authed):\n\n| Extension action | Endpoint | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Load/lazily build draft | `POST /addon/draft` | body `{ iCalUid, providerEventId?, attendees[], title?, start?, end? }` → roster + per-guest status |\n| Persist a host edit | `PATCH /addon/draft` | include toggle / name / phone / templates / location; idempotent; **debounced** from UI |\n| Email preview | `POST /addon/preview` | `{ iCalUid, visitorEmail }` → `{ subject, html, text }`; render `html` in a sandboxed iframe. (GET `/addon/preview-html` also exists for direct iframe src.) |\n| Send (reconcile passes to toggles) | `POST /addon/send` | materialize invites for included guests → per-guest `{ passUrl, status }` |\n| Cancel one guest | `POST /addon/cancel-guest` | `{ iCalUid, invitationId }` |\n\nSend must use the **canonical `iCalUid`** (from Calendar API) so the extension path converges on the same `calendar_event_links` row as `.ics`/OAuth/add-on (spec §6). This is exactly why we chose the Calendar-read approach.\n\n## Design system, theme & motion\n\n- **Port `field-app/src/design/tokens.ts` → web `src/design/tokens.ts`** (strip React Native `Platform`/`TextStyle`; keep the values). Same MD3 scales: primary `#92288E`, `spacing`, `radius`, `type`, `elevation`, `motion` (`fast 120 / base 200 / slow 320`). Expose as CSS custom properties on `:root` + a typed TS object.\n- **Thin component wrappers** (`src/design/components/`): `Button`, `Switch`, `TextField`, `Card`, `DecoratedRow` (the roster-row workhorse), `Chip`, `Skeleton`, `Banner`, `IconButton`. Lucide-react icons only — **no Unicode glyphs/emoji in chrome** (root rule).\n- **Animation rules (honor \"subtle, only where needed\"):** plain **CSS transitions** driven by `motion` tokens — zero runtime cost. Specifically: banner slide+fade in (base), side-panel content fade/slide on load (base), switch thumb + row state-layer transitions (fast), skeleton shimmer, send-success check draw (slow). **No animation library** unless a specific interaction proves it needs one. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n- **Loading UX (root rules):** Skeleton on first paint; keep existing rows visible during background refetch (TanStack Query `keepPreviousData`); inline \"Sending…/Checking…\" with a spinner; never swallow errors — surface the engine's message in plain language.\n\n## Folder structure (WXT)\n\n```\nauxilio-extension/\n  wxt.config.ts                 # manifest: permissions, host_permissions, oauth2, side_panel, action\n  CLAUDE.md  README.md  .gitignore\n  src/\n    entrypoints/\n      background.ts             # SW: token mgr, Calendar client, engine client, per-tab ctx, msg router\n      calendar.content.ts       # content script @ calendar.google.com: detect/observe/inject\n      sidepanel/\n        index.html  main.tsx  App.tsx\n    features/visit/             # the registration UI (roster, toggles, edit, preview, send)\n    lib/\n      auth.ts                   # launchWebAuthFlow + token cache + silent renew\n      calendar.ts               # eid decode + events.get\n      engine.ts                 # typed /addon/* client\n      messaging.ts              # typed runtime-message contracts\n      magic-address.ts          # detect the magic address among attendees/location\n    state/                      # zustand store (session, active event ctx)\n    design/                     # tokens.ts + components/ + global.css (CSS vars)\n```\n\n## Phased build\n\n**Phase 0 — scaffold (1 sitting).** `wxt init` (React+TS), tokens port, design components stub, manifest (permissions: `identity`, `sidePanel`, `storage`; host_permissions: `https://calendar.google.com/*`, engine URL; `oauth2`). Loads unpacked, side panel opens from toolbar icon, \"Hello\" renders with our theme.\n\n**Phase 1 — manual-invoke full flow (the 80% value).** No magic address yet.\n- Content script: detect open event, decode `eid` → `providerEventId`; inject a **\"Register a visitor\"** button into the event view (the user gesture that opens the side panel).\n- Background: mint tokens; Calendar `events.get` → `iCalUid` + attendees; call `/addon/draft`.\n- Side panel: render roster (`DecoratedRow` + `Switch`), inline name/phone edit → debounced `PATCH /addon/draft`; template/location `SelectionInput`; **email preview** in sandboxed iframe via `/addon/preview`; **Send** → `/addon/send` → per-guest success with `passUrl`. TanStack Query optimistic toggles. Honest loading/empty/error states.\n- **End state:** a host opens any event on desktop, clicks the button, curates + previews + sends — entirely in a smooth React panel.\n\n**Phase 2 — magic-address auto-nudge (Option A).**\n- On event open, background fetches the event and `magic-address.ts` checks attendees/location for the magic address (form to confirm against engine ingest — see open questions).\n- If present → content script auto-injects the **dismissible banner** (\"Visitor event — register\"); one click opens the side panel (gesture satisfied). Banner respects dismissal (per-event, `storage.session`).\n- Realtime: `MutationObserver` updates the panel's roster as the host adds/removes guests in the Calendar UI.\n- Optional \"mark as visitor event\" affordance — **writing** the magic address back is deferred (needs a write scope or DOM insertion; decide here, don't pre-build).\n\n**Phase 3 — polish / optional (only on evidence).** FCM backend nudge + toolbar badge (engine already has the watch); write-back \"✓ Registered\" marker; options page (sign-in/out, engine URL); reduced-motion + a11y pass; packaging for public (CWS review + OAuth verification) per the decision doc.\n\n## Open questions (resolve in-flight, don't block scaffold)\n\n- **Magic-address exact form** the extension matches — must equal what the engine ingest keys on (`calendar-ingest.ts` / inbound). Confirm: guest email vs location vs resource.\n- **`eid` → providerEventId parity** with the engine's `iCalUid` dedup — verify the Calendar API `iCalUID` for the same event equals the `.ics` `UID` (spec open question #2).\n- **Silent token renewal** UX if `prompt=none` fails (re-consent banner in panel).\n- **Write-back / magic-address stamping** scope decision (Phase 2/3): client write scope vs DOM insertion vs leave to add-on/manual.\n\n## Verification\n\n- **Load unpacked:** `npm run dev` (WXT) → load `.output/chrome-mv3` in `chrome://extensions`; open Google Calendar, open an event → button/banner appears.\n- **Auth:** trigger `launchWebAuthFlow`, confirm `id_token` aud == the client ID added to the engine env; confirm `/addon/draft` returns a roster (not 401).\n- **Engine end-to-end (against local engine + tunnel, NOT prod):** reuse the engine's dev harness — `ADDON_DEV_TRUST_EMAIL` + `scripts/dev-visitor-http.ts` (spec §7) to exercise `/addon/*` without real tokens first; then real-token path. Verify: open event → draft roster; toggle/exclude + set phone → `PATCH` persists; preview → branded email in iframe; send → 1 invite per included guest, `passUrl` returned; convergence — same event via `.ics` inbound + extension send = one invite per guest (spec §6 regression).\n- **UX bar:** first paint shows skeleton; background refetch keeps rows; toggles feel instant (optimistic); errors show the engine's plain-language message; animations subtle and `prefers-reduced-motion`-aware.\n- **No engine regressions:** `/addon/*` are additive; only `env.updated` changes (audience allow-list). ## Approved Plan:
# Auxilio Calendar Visitor — Chrome Extension (Build Plan)

## Context

We want a **desktop Chrome surface** for registering office visitors directly inside Google Calendar — the richer counterpart to the `auxilio-workspace` add-on. The add-on is mobile-capable but lives under the CardService "card ceiling" (no free-form UI, a server round-trip per interaction, fragile form state). An extension escapes that ceiling: full React UI, realtime in-page reactions, smooth state — the better UX the vision calls for (realtime guest updates, per-guest invite toggle, template preview/select, inline edits, an intentional auto-nudge).

Strategy (locked in `Planning-docs/2026-06-18_calendar_visitor_chrome_extension_decision.md`): **one signal — the magic address — many reactors.** The extension is the desktop reactor; the add-on stays the mobile reactor; the engine remains the OAuth holder + dedup/issuance brain. The extension reuses the engine's **existing** `/api/visitor/calendar/addon/*` contract with **zero engine code changes** — only one env line (add the extension's OAuth client ID to the audience allow-list).

Decisions confirmed with the user:
- **Build tooling: WXT** (batteries-included MV3 over Vite; React 19 + TS).
- **Event data: Calendar read scope.** Extension holds `identity + calendar.events.readonly`; fetches the canonical event by `eid` via the Calendar API for authoritative `iCalUID` + attendees. DOM is used **only for triggers** (detect open, magic address, live edits), never as data-of-record. Internal-first → no OAuth verification yet, no CASA (Calendar-only).

## Repo & stack

- **New independent repo:** sibling folder `auxilio-extension/` with its own `git init` (mirrors how `auxilio-workspace/` is a self-contained sibling). Own `CLAUDE.md`, own remotes later. **Not** Bifrost, **not** EAS.
- **Stack:** WXT + React 19 + TypeScript + Vite (under WXT) + `lucide-react`. **Server state: TanStack Query** (matches visitor-web/ops-dashboard; gives optimistic toggles + background refetch for free). **UI/session/event-context state:** a small Zustand store (tiny, not a UI framework). **No MUI/Tailwind/paper** — our own MD3 tokens + thin component wrappers (per root CLAUDE.md design stance).

## Architecture — four MV3 surfaces

```
content script (calendar.google.com)        side panel (the app)
  • detect event open (URL eid + DOM)         • React + TanStack Query UI
  • detect magic address (via API fetch)      • roster, toggles, edits,
  • inject dismissible banner (Option A)        template select, email preview, send
  • inject "Register visitor" button          • talks to background for token + event ctx
  • read live edits (MutationObserver)                  ▲
            │  runtime msg / port                       │ runtime msg / port
            ▼                                            │
        ┌──────────────────── background service worker ─────────────────┐
        │ • OAuth: mint+cache Google id_token (engine) + access_token (Cal)│
        │ • Calendar API client (events.get by eid → iCalUID, attendees)  │
        │ • engine API client (/addon/draft|patch|preview|send|cancel)    │
        │ • per-tab "active event context" store                          │
        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │ HTTPS (Bearer id_token)
                                   ▼
                    office-ops-engine  /api/visitor/calendar/addon/*
```

**Why this split:** background owns secrets/tokens and all network (one place to verify, thin adapter per umbrella rule). Content script is a dumb trigger/observer. Side panel is pure presentation + server-state.

## Auth model

- `chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow` against Google, **Web OAuth client**, redirect `https://<ext-id>.chromiumapp.org/`, implicit flow `response_type=token id_token`, scopes `openid email profile https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly`.
  - **`id_token`** → sent as `Authorization: Bearer` to the engine (`verifyAddonIdToken` already verifies audience + `email_verified` + domain gate — `office-ops-engine/src/mastra/modules/visitor/addon-auth.ts`).
  - **`access_token`** → Calendar API `events.get` for canonical `iCalUID` + attendees.
- Cache tokens in `chrome.storage.session`; silent re-mint with `prompt=none` on expiry (~1h).
- **Engine change (the only one): add the extension's OAuth client ID to `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`** (comma-list, already supported per spec §3) in `env.updated`. No code change.

## Engine integration — reuse, don't rebuild

All endpoints already exist in `office-ops-engine/src/mastra/modules/visitor/routes.ts` (ID-token authed):

| Extension action | Endpoint | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Load/lazily build draft | `POST /addon/draft` | body `{ iCalUid, providerEventId?, attendees[], title?, start?, end? }` → roster + per-guest status |
| Persist a host edit | `PATCH /addon/draft` | include toggle / name / phone / templates / location; idempotent; **debounced** from UI |
| Email preview | `POST /addon/preview` | `{ iCalUid, visitorEmail }` → `{ subject, html, text }`; render `html` in a sandboxed iframe. (GET `/addon/preview-html` also exists for direct iframe src.) |
| Send (reconcile passes to toggles) | `POST /addon/send` | materialize invites for included guests → per-guest `{ passUrl, status }` |
| Cancel one guest | `POST /addon/cancel-guest` | `{ iCalUid, invitationId }` |

Send must use the **canonical `iCalUid`** (from Calendar API) so the extension path converges on the same `calendar_event_links` row as `.ics`/OAuth/add-on (spec §6). This is exactly why we chose the Calendar-read approach.

## Design system, theme & motion

- **Port `field-app/src/design/tokens.ts` → web `src/design/tokens.ts`** (strip React Native `Platform`/`TextStyle`; keep the values). Same MD3 scales: primary `#92288E`, `spacing`, `radius`, `type`, `elevation`, `motion` (`fast 120 / base 200 / slow 320`). Expose as CSS custom properties on `:root` + a typed TS object.
- **Thin component wrappers** (`src/design/components/`): `Button`, `Switch`, `TextField`, `Card`, `DecoratedRow` (the roster-row workhorse), `Chip`, `Skeleton`, `Banner`, `IconButton`. Lucide-react icons only — **no Unicode glyphs/emoji in chrome** (root rule).
- **Animation rules (honor "subtle, only where needed"):** plain **CSS transitions** driven by `motion` tokens — zero runtime cost. Specifically: banner slide+fade in (base), side-panel content fade/slide on load (base), switch thumb + row state-layer transitions (fast), skeleton shimmer, send-success check draw (slow). **No animation library** unless a specific interaction proves it needs one. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Loading UX (root rules):** Skeleton on first paint; keep existing rows visible during background refetch (TanStack Query `keepPreviousData`); inline "Sending…/Checking…" with a spinner; never swallow errors — surface the engine's message in plain language.

## Folder structure (WXT)

```
auxilio-extension/
  wxt.config.ts                 # manifest: permissions, host_permissions, oauth2, side_panel, action
  CLAUDE.md  README.md  .gitignore
  src/
    entrypoints/
      background.ts             # SW: token mgr, Calendar client, engine client, per-tab ctx, msg router
      calendar.content.ts       # content script @ calendar.google.com: detect/observe/inject
      sidepanel/
        index.html  main.tsx  App.tsx
    features/visit/             # the registration UI (roster, toggles, edit, preview, send)
    lib/
      auth.ts                   # launchWebAuthFlow + token cache + silent renew
      calendar.ts               # eid decode + events.get
      engine.ts                 # typed /addon/* client
      messaging.ts              # typed runtime-message contracts
      magic-address.ts          # detect the magic address among attendees/location
    state/                      # zustand store (session, active event ctx)
    design/                     # tokens.ts + components/ + global.css (CSS vars)
```

## Phased build

**Phase 0 — scaffold (1 sitting).** `wxt init` (React+TS), tokens port, design components stub, manifest (permissions: `identity`, `sidePanel`, `storage`; host_permissions: `https://calendar.google.com/*`, engine URL; `oauth2`). Loads unpacked, side panel opens from toolbar icon, "Hello" renders with our theme.

**Phase 1 — manual-invoke full flow (the 80% value).** No magic address yet.
- Content script: detect open event, decode `eid` → `providerEventId`; inject a **"Register a visitor"** button into the event view (the user gesture that opens the side panel).
- Background: mint tokens; Calendar `events.get` → `iCalUid` + attendees; call `/addon/draft`.
- Side panel: render roster (`DecoratedRow` + `Switch`), inline name/phone edit → debounced `PATCH /addon/draft`; template/location `SelectionInput`; **email preview** in sandboxed iframe via `/addon/preview`; **Send** → `/addon/send` → per-guest success with `passUrl`. TanStack Query optimistic toggles. Honest loading/empty/error states.
- **End state:** a host opens any event on desktop, clicks the button, curates + previews + sends — entirely in a smooth React panel.

**Phase 2 — magic-address auto-nudge (Option A).**
- On event open, background fetches the event and `magic-address.ts` checks attendees/location for the magic address (form to confirm against engine ingest — see open questions).
- If present → content script auto-injects the **dismissible banner** ("Visitor event — register"); one click opens the side panel (gesture satisfied). Banner respects dismissal (per-event, `storage.session`).
- Realtime: `MutationObserver` updates the panel's roster as the host adds/removes guests in the Calendar UI.
- Optional "mark as visitor event" affordance — **writing** the magic address back is deferred (needs a write scope or DOM insertion; decide here, don't pre-build).

**Phase 3 — polish / optional (only on evidence).** FCM backend nudge + toolbar badge (engine already has the watch); write-back "✓ Registered" marker; options page (sign-in/out, engine URL); reduced-motion + a11y pass; packaging for public (CWS review + OAuth verification) per the decision doc.

## Open questions (resolve in-flight, don't block scaffold)

- **Magic-address exact form** the extension matches — must equal what the engine ingest keys on (`calendar-ingest.ts` / inbound). Confirm: guest email vs location vs resource.
- **`eid` → providerEventId parity** with the engine's `iCalUid` dedup — verify the Calendar API `iCalUID` for the same event equals the `.ics` `UID` (spec open question #2).
- **Silent token renewal** UX if `prompt=none` fails (re-consent banner in panel).
- **Write-back / magic-address stamping** scope decision (Phase 2/3): client write scope vs DOM insertion vs leave to add-on/manual.

## Verification

- **Load unpacked:** `npm run dev` (WXT) → load `.output/chrome-mv3` in `chrome://extensions`; open Google Calendar, open an event → button/banner appears.
- **Auth:** trigger `launchWebAuthFlow`, confirm `id_token` aud == the client ID added to the engine env; confirm `/addon/draft` returns a roster (not 401).
- **Engine end-to-end (against local engine + tunnel, NOT prod):** reuse the engine's dev harness — `ADDON_DEV_TRUST_EMAIL` + `scripts/dev-visitor-http.ts` (spec §7) to exercise `/addon/*` without real tokens first; then real-token path. Verify: open event → draft roster; toggle/exclude + set phone → `PATCH` persists; preview → branded email in iframe; send → 1 invite per included guest, `passUrl` returned; convergence — same event via `.ics` inbound + extension send = one invite per guest (spec §6 regression).
- **UX bar:** first paint shows skeleton; background refetch keeps rows; toggles feel instant (optimistic); errors show the engine's plain-language message; animations subtle and `prefers-reduced-motion`-aware.
- **No engine regressions:** `/addon/*` are additive; only `env.updated` changes (audience allow-list). Do not touch `/api/visitor/invite`, Slack, or visitor-web routes.

## Guardrails

- Calendar-only scopes — **never** add Gmail/Drive (CASA line, same as add-on).
- Background is the only secret/token/network holder; content script stays a dumb trigger; side panel stays presentation — keep the thin-adapter boundary.
- No engine signature/scope changes; no widening the shared per-user OAuth (reconnect-storm rule).
- Don't commit secrets (OAuth client config via env/build-time, not hardcoded).

```

}

  "content": "import type { ButtonHTMLAttributes, ReactNode } from 'react';\nimport { Spinner } from './Spinner';\n\ntype Variant = 'filled' | 'tonal' | 'text' | 'danger';\n\ninterface ButtonProps extends ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> {\n  variant?: Variant;\n  block?: boolean;\n  loading?: boolean;\n  icon?: ReactNode;\n}\n\n/** Thin MD3 button wrapper. Styling lives in global.css (.btn*). */\nexport function Button({\n  variant = 'filled',\n  block,\n  loading,\n  icon,\n  children,\n  disabled,\n  className,\n  ...rest\n}: ButtonProps) {\n  const classes = [\n    'btn',\n    `btn--${variant}`,\n    block ? 'btn--block' : '',\n    className ?? '',\n  ]\n    .filter(Boolean)\n    .join(' ');\n\n  return (\n    <button className={classes} disabled={disabled || loading} {...rest}>\n      {loading ? <Spinner /> : icon}\n      {children}\n    </button>\n  );\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import React from 'react';\nimport ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';\nimport { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';\nimport App from './App';\nimport '@/design/global.css';\n\n// Server state lives in TanStack Query: optimistic toggles + background refetch.\nconst queryClient = new QueryClient({\n  defaultOptions: {\n    queries: { retry: 1, staleTime: 30_000, refetchOnWindowFocus: false },\n  },\n});\n\nReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(\n  <React.StrictMode>\n    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>\n      <App />\n    </QueryClientProvider>\n  </React.StrictMode>,\n);\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/appointy/work/OfficeOperationsUmbrella/auxilio-extension/CLAUDE.md",
  "content": "# auxilio-extension\n\nGoogle **Chrome extension (MV3)** for Auxilio (Office Ops) — the **desktop** surface for registering office visitors directly inside Google Calendar. It is the richer counterpart to the `auxilio-workspace` Calendar add-on: where the add-on is mobile-capable but lives under the CardService \"card ceiling,\" the extension gives a full React UI (realtime guest updates, per-guest invite toggle, template preview, inline edits, intentional auto-nudge).\n\n> Read the umbrella `../CLAUDE.md` for the four constraints and UX rules — they apply here.\n> Strategy + approval analysis: `../Planning-docs/2026-06-18_calendar_visitor_chrome_extension_decision.md`.\n> Build plan: the approved plan that scaffolded this repo.\n\n## What this is (and isn't)\n\n- **Is:** an MV3 extension (WXT + React 19 + TS) that injects a trigger into Google Calendar (web) and renders the registration flow in the **side panel**. A **channel surface / dumb adapter** — it forwards intent to `office-ops-engine`.\n- **Isn't:** a place for business logic. Dedup, draft curation, invite/pass issuance, and lifecycle all live in `office-ops-engine`'s visitor plugin. This repo renders UI and calls the engine.\n- **Isn't:** mobile. Extensions are desktop-Chrome only. The `auxilio-workspace` add-on remains the mobile surface. Both key off the same **magic address**.\n\n## Architecture — three MV3 surfaces\n\n- **`entrypoints/background.ts`** (service worker) — the only holder of tokens + network. Mints/caches the Google `id_token` (engine auth) + `access_token` (Calendar read), runs the Calendar API client and the engine `/addon/*` client, keeps per-tab event context, routes messages.\n- **`entrypoints/calendar.content.ts`** (content script @ `calendar.google.com`) — a **dumb trigger/observer**: detect open event, decode `eid`, inject the \"Register a visitor\" button (Phase 1) and the magic-address banner (Phase 2). No tokens, no business logic.\n- **`entrypoints/sidepanel/`** (the app) — React + TanStack Query UI. Pure presentation + server state.\n\n```\ncontent script ──msg──> background ──HTTPS(id_token)──> office-ops-engine /api/visitor/calendar/addon/*\nside panel    ──msg──> background ──Calendar API(access_token)──> canonical iCalUID + attendees\n```\n\n## Hard rules\n\n1. **Calendar-only scopes. Never add Gmail/Drive.** Calendar is *sensitive* (verification, no paid audit). Gmail/Drive are *restricted* → annual CASA assessment. Hard line, same as the add-on.\n2. **Engine owns the contract.** The extension calls the existing `/api/visitor/calendar/addon/{draft,preview,send,cancel-guest}` routes (ID-token authed). Do **not** add engine signature/scope changes from here. The only engine-side change is env: add this extension's OAuth client id to `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` (audience allow-list).\n3. **Background is the only secret/network holder.** Content script stays a dumb trigger; side panel stays presentation. Keep the thin-adapter boundary.\n4. **Send the canonical `iCalUID`** (from the Calendar API `events.get`, not synthesized) so the extension path converges on the same `calendar_event_links` row as `.ics`/OAuth/add-on.\n5. **Design: Material 3 tokens, not its code.** Our own `design/tokens.ts` + `global.css` (primary `#92288E`). No MUI/Tailwind/paper. **Icons: lucide-react only**, no Unicode glyphs/emoji in chrome.\n6. **Animations subtle, only where needed** — CSS transitions driven by motion tokens; respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n7. **Internal-first.** Force-installed/unlisted to our Workspace → no OAuth verification yet. Public/commercial = a later packaging + verification exercise (CWS review + OAuth verification), per the decision doc.\n\n## Stack & commands\n\nWXT (MV3 over Vite) + React 19 + TypeScript + TanStack Query (server state) + Zustand (UI/session/event-context) + lucide-react.\n\n```bash\nnpm install\nnpm run dev        # WXT dev server; load .output/chrome-mv3 in chrome://extensions (Developer mode → Load unpacked)\nnpm run build      # production build → .output/chrome-mv3\nnpm run compile    # tsc --noEmit (type-check)\nnpm run zip        # packaged zip for store upload\n```\n\nEnv: copy `.env.example` → `.env` (engine URL, OAuth client id, magic address). `WXT_` vars are inlined at build.\n\n## Deploy / distribution\n\n**Not Bifrost, not EAS.** Internal-first via Chrome admin **force-install** (unlisted, by extension id) or \"Load unpacked\" for dev. Public later via the Chrome Web Store (payments handled by our own engine; CWS no longer bills).\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/appointy/work/OfficeOperationsUmbrella/auxilio-extension/lib/messaging.ts",
  "content": "/**\n * Typed RPC over chrome.runtime messaging. The side panel (and content script)\n * never touch tokens or the network directly — they send these messages and the\n * background worker does the work. This keeps the thin-adapter boundary: one\n * place holds secrets + network.\n */\nimport type {\n  ActiveEvent,\n  AuthStatus,\n  DraftPatch,\n  DraftResponse,\n  PreviewResponse,\n  SendResponse,\n  VisitDraft,\n} from './types';\n\nexport type RpcRequest =\n  | { type: 'AUTH_STATUS' }\n  | { type: 'AUTH_SIGN_IN' }\n  | { type: 'AUTH_SIGN_OUT' }\n  | { type: 'OPEN_FOR_EVENT'; eid: string }\n  | { type: 'GET_ACTIVE_EVENT' }\n  | { type: 'DRAFT_LOAD'; event: ActiveEvent }\n  | { type: 'DRAFT_PATCH'; iCalUid: string; patch: DraftPatch }\n  | { type: 'PREVIEW'; iCalUid: string; visitorEmail: string }\n  | { type: 'SEND'; iCalUid: string; start?: string; end?: string }\n  | { type: 'CANCEL_GUEST'; iCalUid: string; invitationId: string };\n\n/** Maps each request type to its success payload. */\nexport interface RpcResultMap {\n  AUTH_STATUS: AuthStatus;\n  AUTH_SIGN_IN: AuthStatus;\n  AUTH_SIGN_OUT: { signedIn: false };\n  OPEN_FOR_EVENT: { opened: boolean };\n  GET_ACTIVE_EVENT: ActiveEvent | null;\n  DRAFT_LOAD: DraftResponse;\n  DRAFT_PATCH: VisitDraft;\n  PREVIEW: PreviewResponse;\n  SEND: SendResponse;\n  CANCEL_GUEST: { invitationId: string; cancelled: boolean };\n}\n\nexport type RpcResponse<T> =\n  | { ok: true; data: T }\n  | { ok: false; error: string; status?: number; needsAuth?: boolean };\n\nexport class RpcError extends Error {\n  constructor(\n    message: string,\n    readonly status?: number,\n    readonly needsAuth?: boolean,\n  ) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'RpcError';\n  }\n}\n\n/** Side-panel-side caller: throws RpcError on failure, returns typed data. */\nexport async function rpc<K extends RpcRequest['type']>(\n  msg: Extract<RpcRequest, { type: K }>,\n): Promise<RpcResultMap[K]> {\n  const res = (await chrome.runtime.sendMessage(msg)) as\n    | RpcResponse<RpcResultMap[K]>\n    | undefined;\n  if (!res) throw new RpcError('No response from background worker');\n  if (!res.ok) throw new RpcError(res.error, res.status, res.needsAuth);\n  return res.data;\n}\n\n/** Storage key for the globally-active event (set by background, read by panel). */\nexport const ACTIVE_EVENT_KEY = 'auxilio.activeEvent';\n"
}

{

  "content": "/**\n * Auth (background only). Mints a Google id_token (engine auth) + access_token\n * (Calendar read) via chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow against a Web OAuth\n * client, caches them in storage.session, and silently re-mints on expiry.\n *\n * The id_token's audience must be on the engine's AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID\n * allow-list. Calendar-only scopes (no Gmail/Drive — CASA line).\n */\nimport { OAUTH_CLIENT_ID } from './config';\nimport type { AuthStatus } from './types';\n\nconst SCOPES = [\n  'openid',\n  'email',\n  'profile',\n  'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly',\n].join(' ');\n\nconst KEY = 'auxilio.tokens';\n\ninterface TokenBundle {\n  idToken: string;\n  accessToken: string;\n  email?: string;\n  expiresAt: number;\n}\n\nfunction parseFragment(redirectUrl: string) {\n  const params = new URLSearchParams(new URL(redirectUrl).hash.slice(1));\n  return {\n    accessToken: params.get('access_token') ?? '',\n    idToken: params.get('id_token') ?? '',\n    expiresIn: Number(params.get('expires_in') ?? '3600'),\n    error: params.get('error') ?? undefined,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction emailFromIdToken(idToken: string): string | undefined {\n  try {\n    const part = idToken.split('.')[1].replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');\n    return JSON.parse(atob(part)).email as string | undefined;\n  } catch {\n    return undefined;\n  }\n}\n\nasync function readCache(): Promise<TokenBundle | null> {\n  const r = await chrome.storage.session.get(KEY);\n  return (r[KEY] as TokenBundle) ?? null;\n}\n\nasync function mint(interactive: boolean): Promise<TokenBundle> {\n  if (!OAUTH_CLIENT_ID) {\n    throw new Error(\n      'OAuth client id missing. Set WXT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID in .env and rebuild.',\n    );\n  }\n  const url = new URL('https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth');\n  url.searchParams.set('client_id', OAUTH_CLIENT_ID);\n  url.searchParams.set('response_type', 'token id_token');\n  url.searchParams.set('redirect_uri', chrome.identity.getRedirectURL());\n  url.searchParams.set('scope', SCOPES);\n  url.searchParams.set('nonce', crypto.randomUUID());\n  url.searchParams.set('prompt', interactive ? 'consent select_account' : 'none');\n\n  const redirect = await chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow({\n    url: url.toString(),\n    interactive,\n  });\n  if (!redirect) throw new Error('Sign-in was cancelled');\n\n  const { accessToken, idToken, expiresIn, error } = parseFragment(redirect);\n  if (error) throw new Error(`Google sign-in error: ${error}`);\n  if (!idToken || !accessToken) throw new Error('Sign-in did not return tokens');\n\n  const bundle: TokenBundle = {\n    idToken,\n    accessToken,\n    email: emailFromIdToken(idToken),\n    expiresAt: Date.now() + (expiresIn - 60) * 1000, // refresh 60s early\n  };\n  await chrome.storage.session.set({ [KEY]: bundle });\n  return bundle;\n}\n\n/** Valid tokens, silently re-minting if expired. Throws if interactive sign-in\n *  is required (caller surfaces a sign-in gate). */\nexport async function getValidTokens(): Promise<TokenBundle> {\n  const cached = await readCache();\n  if (cached && cached.expiresAt > Date.now()) return cached;\n  return mint(false); // prompt=none silent renew\n}\n\nexport async function signIn(): Promise<AuthStatus> {\n  const bundle = await mint(true);\n  return { signedIn: true, email: bundle.email };\n}\n\nexport async function signOut(): Promise<void> {\n  const cached = await readCache();\n  if (cached?.accessToken) {\n    await fetch(\n      `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke?token=${cached.accessToken}`,\n      { method: 'POST' },\n    ).catch(() => {});\n  }\n  await chrome.storage.session.remove(KEY);\n}\n\nexport async function authStatus(): Promise<AuthStatus> {\n  const cached = await readCache();\n  if (cached && cached.expiresAt > Date.now()) {\n    return { signedIn: true, email: cached.email };\n  }\n  return { signedIn: false };\n}\n"
}

{

  "content": "/**\n * Calendar read (background only). Decodes the Google Calendar `eid` from the\n * page URL and fetches the canonical event via the Calendar API so we work from\n * authoritative iCalUID + attendees (not scraped DOM). Calendar.events.readonly.\n */\nimport type { ActiveEvent } from './types';\n\n/** `eid` is URL-safe base64 of \"<eventId> <calendarId>\" (calendarId optional). */\nexport function decodeEid(eid: string): { eventId: string; calendarId: string } | null {\n  try {\n    let b64 = eid.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');\n    b64 += '='.repeat((4 - (b64.length % 4)) % 4);\n    const decoded = atob(b64);\n    const [eventId, calendarId] = decoded.split(' ');\n    if (!eventId) return null;\n    return { eventId, calendarId: calendarId || 'primary' };\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\ninterface GCalEvent {\n  iCalUID?: string;\n  summary?: string;\n  location?: string;\n  start?: { dateTime?: string; date?: string };\n  end?: { dateTime?: string; date?: string };\n  organizer?: { email?: string };\n  attendees?: {\n    email?: string;\n    displayName?: string;\n    resource?: boolean;\n    self?: boolean;\n    organizer?: boolean;\n  }[];\n}\n\nexport async function fetchActiveEvent(\n  eid: string,\n  accessToken: string,\n): Promise<ActiveEvent> {\n  const dec = decodeEid(eid);\n  if (!dec) throw new Error('Could not read the event id from this page.');\n\n  const url = new URL(\n    `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/${encodeURIComponent(\n      dec.calendarId,\n    )}/events/${encodeURIComponent(dec.eventId)}`,\n  );\n  url.searchParams.set(\n    'fields',\n    'iCalUID,summary,location,start,end,organizer,attendees(email,displayName,resource,self,organizer)',\n  );\n\n  const res = await fetch(url, {\n    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },\n  });\n  if (!res.ok) {\n    if (res.status === 404) {\n      throw new Error('This event was not found on your calendar.');\n    }\n    throw new Error(`Calendar API error (${res.status}).`);\n  }\n  const ev = (await res.json()) as GCalEvent;\n\n  const attendees = (ev.attendees ?? [])\n    .filter((a) => a.email && !a.resource)\n    .map((a) => ({ email: a.email as string, name: a.displayName }));\n\n  return {\n    iCalUid: ev.iCalUID ?? '',\n    providerEventId: dec.eventId,\n    title: ev.summary,\n    start: ev.start?.dateTime ?? ev.start?.date,\n    end: ev.end?.dateTime ?? ev.end?.date,\n    location: ev.location,\n    organizerEmail: ev.organizer?.email,\n    attendees,\n  };\n}\n"
}

Always sends the canonical iCalUid so the\n * extension converges on the same calendar_event_links row as .ics/OAuth/add-on.\n */\nimport { ADDON_API } from './config';\nimport type {\n  ActiveEvent,\n  DraftPatch,\n  DraftResponse,\n  PreviewResponse,\n  SendResponse,\n  VisitDraft,\n} from './types';\n\nexport class EngineError extends Error {\n  constructor(\n    message: string,\n    readonly status: number,\n  ) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'EngineError';\n  }\n}\n\nasync function call<T>(\n  path: string,\n  method: string,\n  idToken: string,\n  body?: unknown,\n): Promise<T> {\n  const res = await fetch(`${ADDON_API}/${path}`, {\n    method,\n    headers: {\n      'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n      Authorization: `Bearer ${idToken}`,\n    },\n    body: body ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,\n  });\n  const text = await res.text();\n  const data = text ? JSON.parse(text) : {};\n  if (!res.ok) {\n    throw new EngineError(data?.error ?? `Request failed (${res.status})`, res.status);\n  }\n  return data as T;\n}\n\nexport const engine = {\n  loadDraft: (idToken: string, ev: ActiveEvent) =>\n    call<DraftResponse>('draft', 'POST', idToken, {\n      iCalUid: ev.iCalUid,\n      providerEventId: ev.providerEventId,\n      title: ev.title,\n      attendees: ev.attendees,\n      start: ev.start,\n      end: ev.end,\n      location: ev.location,\n      organizerEmail: ev.organizerEmail,\n    }),\n\n  patchDraft: (idToken: string, iCalUid: string, patch: DraftPatch) =>\n    call<VisitDraft>('draft', 'PATCH', idToken, { iCalUid, patch }),\n\n  preview: (idToken: string, iCalUid: string, visitorEmail: string) =>\n    call<PreviewResponse>('preview', 'POST', idToken, { iCalUid, visitorEmail }),\n\n  send: (idToken: string, iCalUid: string, start?: string, end?: string) =>\n    call<SendResponse>('send', 'POST', idToken, { iCalUid, start, end }),\n\n  cancelGuest: (idToken: string, iCalUid: string, invitationId: string) =>\n    call<{ invitationId: string; cancelled: boolean }>(\n      'cancel-guest',\n      'POST',\n      idToken,\n      { iCalUid, invitationId },\n    ),\n};\n"
}

  "content": "import {\n  ACTIVE_EID_KEY,\n  type RpcRequest,\n  type RpcResponse,\n} from '@/lib/messaging';\nimport { authStatus, getValidTokens, signIn, signOut } from '@/lib/auth';\nimport { fetchActiveEvent } from '@/lib/calendar';\nimport { EngineError, engine } from '@/lib/engine';\n\nexport default defineBackground(() => {\n  // Toolbar icon opens the panel (Chrome's required user gesture).\n  chrome.sidePanel\n    .setPanelBehavior({ openPanelOnActionClick: true })\n    .catch((err) => console.error('[auxilio] setPanelBehavior failed', err));\n\n  chrome.runtime.onMessage.addListener((msg: RpcRequest, sender, sendResponse) => {\n    handle(msg, sender)\n      .then(sendResponse)\n      .catch((err) => sendResponse(fail(err)));\n    return true; // async response\n  });\n\n  console.log('[auxilio] background ready');\n});\n\nconst ok = <T,>(data: T): RpcResponse<T> => ({ ok: true, data });\n\nfunction fail(err: unknown): RpcResponse<never> {\n  const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n  const status = err instanceof EngineError ? err.status : undefined;\n  const needsAuth = status === 401;\n  return { ok: false, error: message, status, needsAuth };\n}\n\n/** Run an engine call with a fresh id_token; map auth failures to needsAuth. */\nasync function withIdToken<T>(\n  fn: (idToken: string) => Promise<T>,\n): Promise<RpcResponse<T>> {\n  let idToken: string;\n  try {\n    idToken = (await getValidTokens()).idToken;\n  } catch {\n    return { ok: false, error: 'Sign in to continue.', needsAuth: true };\n  }\n  try {\n    return ok(await fn(idToken));\n  } catch (err) {\n    return fail(err);\n  }\n}\n\nasync function handle(\n  msg: RpcRequest,\n  sender: chrome.runtime.MessageSender,\n): Promise<RpcResponse<unknown>> {\n  switch (msg.type) {\n    case 'AUTH_STATUS':\n      return ok(await authStatus());\n    case 'AUTH_SIGN_IN':\n      return ok(await signIn());\n    case 'AUTH_SIGN_OUT':\n      await signOut();\n      return ok({ signedIn: false });\n\n    case 'OPEN_FOR_EVENT': {\n      // Store the pending event id, then open the panel using the gesture that\n      // came with this content-script click. Resolution/auth happens in the panel.\n      await chrome.storage.session.set({ [ACTIVE_EID_KEY]: msg.eid });\n      let opened = false;\n      try {\n        const tabId = sender.tab?.id;\n        if (tabId != null) {\n          await chrome.sidePanel.open({ tabId });\n          opened = true;\n        }\n      } catch {\n        // Gesture may not have carried; the user can click the toolbar icon.\n      }\n      return ok({ opened });\n    }\n\n    case 'RESOLVE_EVENT':\n      return withIdToken(async () => {\n        const tokens = await getValidTokens();\n        return fetchActiveEvent(msg.eid, tokens.accessToken);\n      });\n\n    case 'DRAFT_LOAD':\n      return withIdToken((t) => engine.loadDraft(t, msg.event));\n    case 'DRAFT_PATCH':\n      return withIdToken((t) => engine.patchDraft(t, msg.iCalUid, msg.patch));\n    case 'PREVIEW':\n      return withIdToken((t) => engine.preview(t, msg.iCalUid, msg.visitorEmail));\n    case 'SEND':\n      return withIdToken((t) => engine.send(t, msg.iCalUid, msg.start, msg.end));\n    case 'CANCEL_GUEST':\n      return withIdToken((t) =>\n        engine.cancelGuest(t, msg.iCalUid, msg.invitationId),\n      );\n\n    default:\n      return { ok: false, error: 'Unknown request' };\n  }\n}\n"
}

(Phase 2 adds the magic-address banner.)\n */\nimport { MAGIC_ADDRESS } from '@/lib/config'; // reserved for Phase 2\n\nconst PRIMARY = '#92288e';\n\nexport default defineContentScript({\n  matches: ['https://calendar.google.com/*'],\n  main() {\n    void MAGIC_ADDRESS; // referenced in Phase 2; keep the import wired\n    const ui = mountTrigger();\n    let lastEid: string | null = null;\n\n    const sync = () => {\n      const eid = currentEid();\n      if (eid === lastEid) return;\n      lastEid = eid;\n      ui.setEid(eid);\n    };\n\n    sync();\n    // Calendar is an SPA; poll the URL (cheap) instead of coupling to its DOM.\n    setInterval(sync, 700);\n    window.addEventListener('popstate', sync);\n\n    console.log('[auxilio] content script ready on Google Calendar');\n  },\n});\n\n/** Extract the Google Calendar event id from the current URL, if an event is open. */\nfunction currentEid(): string | null {\n  const path = location.pathname.match(/\\/eventedit\\/([^/?#]+)/);\n  if (path) return safeDecode(path[1]);\n  const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('eid');\n  return q ? safeDecode(q) : null;\n}\n\nfunction safeDecode(s: string): string {\n  try {\n    return decodeURIComponent(s);\n  } catch {\n    return s;\n  }\n}\n\nconst USER_PLUS_SVG = `\n<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"20\" height=\"20\" viewBox=\"0 0 24 24\"\n  fill=\"none\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"2.2\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\">\n  <path d=\"M16 21v-2a4 4 0 0 0-4-4H6a4 4 0 0 0-4 4v2\"/>\n  <circle cx=\"9\" cy=\"7\" r=\"4\"/>\n  <line x1=\"19\" x2=\"19\" y1=\"8\" y2=\"14\"/>\n  <line x1=\"22\" x2=\"16\" y1=\"11\" y2=\"11\"/>\n</svg>`;\n\n/** Inject a shadow-DOM floating button. Returns a handle to toggle visibility. */\nfunction mountTrigger() {\n  const host = document.createElement('div');\n  host.id = 'auxilio-trigger-host';\n  host.style.cssText =\n    'position:fixed;right:24px;bottom:24px;z-index:2147483646;';\n  document.documentElement.appendChild(host);\n\n  const root = host.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });\n  root.innerHTML = `\n    <style>\n      :host { all: initial; }\n      .fab {\n        display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;\n        font-family: 'Google Sans','Roboto',system-ui,sans-serif;\n        font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .1px;\n        color: #fff; background: ${PRIMARY};\n        border: none; border-radius: 999px; padding: 12px 18px;\n        box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.18); cursor: pointer;\n        transform: translateY(8px); opacity: 0; pointer-events: none;\n        transition: opacity 200ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1),\n                    transform 200ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1),\n                    box-shadow 120ms ease;\n      }\n      .fab.show { opacity: 1; transform: none; pointer-events: auto; }\n      .fab:hover { box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.24); }\n      .fab:active { transform: scale(.98); }\n      .fab[disabled] { opacity: .6; pointer-events: none; }\n      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\n        .fab { transition: none; transform: none; }\n      }\n    </style>\n    <button class=\"fab\" type=\"button\" part=\"fab\">\n      ${USER_PLUS_SVG}<span class=\"label\">Register a visitor</span>\n    </button>`;\n\n  const btn = root.querySelector('button.fab') as HTMLButtonElement;\n  const label = root.querySelector('.label') as HTMLSpanElement;\n  let eid: string | null = null;\n\n  btn.addEventListener('click', async () => {\n    if (!eid) return;\n    btn.disabled = true;\n    label.textContent = 'Opening…';\n    try {\n      await chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ type: 'OPEN_FOR_EVENT', eid });\n    } catch (err) {\n      console.error('[auxilio] open failed', err);\n    } finally {\n      btn.disabled = false;\n      label.textContent = 'Register a visitor';\n    }\n  });\n\n  return {\n    setEid(next: string | null) {\n      eid = next;\n      btn.classList.toggle('show', !!next);\n    },\n  };\n}\n"
}

'@/lib/messaging';\nimport type {\n  ActiveEvent,\n  AuthStatus,\n  DraftPatch,\n  DraftResponse,\n  VisitDraft,\n} from '@/lib/types';\n\n/** The pending event id, read reactively from storage.session. */\nexport function useActiveEid(): string | null {\n  const [eid, setEid] = useState<string | null>(null);\n  useEffect(() => {\n    chrome.storage.session\n      .get(ACTIVE_EID_KEY)\n      .then((r) => setEid((r[ACTIVE_EID_KEY] as string) ?? null));\n    const listener = (\n      changes: { [k: string]: chrome.storage.StorageChange },\n      area: string,\n    ) => {\n      if (area === 'session' && changes[ACTIVE_EID_KEY]) {\n        setEid((changes[ACTIVE_EID_KEY].newValue as string) ?? null);\n      }\n    };\n    chrome.storage.onChanged.addListener(listener);\n    return () => chrome.storage.onChanged.removeListener(listener);\n  }, []);\n  return eid;\n}\n\nexport function useAuthStatus() {\n  return useQuery({\n    queryKey: ['auth'],\n    queryFn: () => rpc({ type: 'AUTH_STATUS' }),\n  });\n}\n\nexport function useSignIn() {\n  const qc = useQueryClient();\n  return useMutation({\n    mutationFn: () => rpc({ type: 'AUTH_SIGN_IN' }),\n    onSuccess: (status: AuthStatus) => {\n      qc.setQueryData(['auth'], status);\n      // re-run any failed queries now that we're signed in\n      qc.invalidateQueries();\n    },\n  });\n}\n\nexport function useResolveEvent(eid: string | null) {\n  return useQuery({\n    queryKey: ['resolve', eid],\n    queryFn: () => rpc({ type: 'RESOLVE_EVENT', eid: eid! }),\n    enabled: !!eid,\n    staleTime: 60_000,\n  });\n}\n\nexport function useDraft(event: ActiveEvent | undefined) {\n  return useQuery({\n    queryKey: ['draft', event?.iCalUid],\n    queryFn: () => rpc({ type: 'DRAFT_LOAD', event: event! }),\n    enabled: !!event?.iCalUid,\n  });\n}\n\n/** Merge a returned VisitDraft into the cached DraftResponse (keep extras). */\nfunction mergeDraft(\n  prev: DraftResponse | undefined,\n  next: VisitDraft,\n): DraftResponse | undefined {\n  if (!prev) return prev;\n  return { ...prev, ...next };\n}\n\n/** Optimistic patch (toggle / name / phone / template / location). */\nexport function usePatchDraft(iCalUid: string | undefined) {\n  const qc = useQueryClient();\n  const key = ['draft', iCalUid];\n  return useMutation({\n    mutationFn: (patch: DraftPatch) =>\n      rpc({ type: 'DRAFT_PATCH', iCalUid: iCalUid!, patch }),\n    onMutate: async (patch) => {\n      await qc.cancelQueries({ queryKey: key });\n      const prev = qc.getQueryData<DraftResponse>(key);\n      if (prev) qc.setQueryData<DraftResponse>(key, applyPatch(prev, patch));\n      return { prev };\n    },\n    onError: (_e, _patch, ctx) => {\n      if (ctx?.prev) qc.setQueryData(key, ctx.prev);\n    },\n    onSuccess: (updated) => {\n      qc.setQueryData<DraftResponse>(key, (prev) => mergeDraft(prev, updated));\n    },\n  });\n}\n\n/** Apply a DraftPatch to a cached DraftResponse for the optimistic view. */\nfunction applyPatch(draft: DraftResponse, patch: DraftPatch): DraftResponse {\n  const roster = draft.roster.map((g) => {\n    const edit = patch.guests?.find(\n      (e) => e.email.toLowerCase() === g.email.toLowerCase(),\n    );\n    return edit ? { ...g, ...stripEmail(edit) } : g;\n  });\n  return {\n    ...draft,\n    roster,\n    location: patch.location ?? draft.location,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction stripEmail<T extends { email: string }>(e: T): Omit<T, 'email'> {\n  const { email: _email, ...rest } = e;\n  return rest;\n}\n\nexport function useSend(iCalUid: string | undefined, start?: string, end?: string) {\n  const qc = useQueryClient();\n  return useMutation({\n    mutationFn: () => rpc({ type: 'SEND', iCalUid: iCalUid!, start, end }),\n    onSuccess: (res) => {\n      qc.setQueryData<DraftResponse>(['draft', iCalUid], (prev) =>\n        mergeDraft(prev, res.draft),\n      );\n    },\n  });\n}\n\nexport function usePreview(iCalUid: string | undefined) {\n  return useMutation({\n    mutationFn: (visitorEmail: string) =>\n      rpc({ type: 'PREVIEW', iCalUid: iCalUid!, visitorEmail }),\n  });\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\nimport { Eye } from 'lucide-react';\nimport { Chip, IconButton, SelectField, Spinner, Switch, TextField } from '@/design/components';\nimport type { DraftGuest, EmailTemplate } from '@/lib/types';\n\ntype GuestEdit = {\n  include?: boolean;\n  name?: string;\n  phone?: string;\n  emailTemplateKey?: string;\n};\n\nexport function RosterRow({\n  guest,\n  templates,\n  onChange,\n  onPreview,\n  previewing,\n}: {\n  guest: DraftGuest;\n  templates: EmailTemplate[];\n  onChange: (edit: GuestEdit) => void;\n  onPreview: () => void;\n  previewing: boolean;\n}) {\n  const [name, setName] = useState(guest.name);\n  const [phone, setPhone] = useState(guest.phone ?? '');\n\n  // Keep local inputs in sync when the server reconciles the row.\n  useEffect(() => setName(guest.name), [guest.name]);\n  useEffect(() => setPhone(guest.phone ?? ''), [guest.phone]);\n\n  const sent = guest.status === 'sent';\n  const cancelled = guest.status === 'cancelled';\n  const defaultTemplate = templates.find((t) => t.isDefault)?.key ?? templates[0]?.key;\n\n  return (\n    <div className={`row${guest.include ? '' : ' row--dim'}`}>\n      <Switch\n        checked={guest.include}\n        disabled={sent}\n        onChange={(v) => onChange({ include: v })}\n        label={`Invite ${guest.email}`}\n      />\n\n      <div className=\"row__grow\">\n        <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>\n          <span className=\"type-label row__ellipsis\" style={{ flex: '0 1 auto' }}>\n            {guest.name || guest.email}\n          </span>\n          {guest.internal && !sent && <Chip>Internal</Chip>}\n          {sent && <Chip tone=\"success\">Pass sent</Chip>}\n          {cancelled && <Chip tone=\"error\">Cancelled</Chip>}\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"type-label-sm text-muted row__ellipsis\">{guest.email}</div>\n\n        {guest.include && !sent && (\n          <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8, marginTop: 10 }}>\n            <TextField\n              label=\"Visitor name\"\n              value={name}\n              onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)}\n              onBlur={() => name !== guest.name && onChange({ name })}\n              placeholder=\"Full name\"\n            />\n            <TextField\n              label=\"Phone (for WhatsApp pass)\"\n              value={phone}\n              inputMode=\"tel\"\n              onChange={(e) => setPhone(e.target.value)}\n              onBlur={() => phone !== (guest.phone ?? '') && onChange({ phone })}\n              placeholder=\"+91…\"\n            />\n            {templates.length >= 2 && (\n              <SelectField\n                label=\"Email template\"\n                value={guest.emailTemplateKey ?? defaultTemplate}\n                onChange={(e) => onChange({ emailTemplateKey: e.target.value })}\n              >\n                {templates.map((t) => (\n                  <option key={t.key} value={t.key}>\n                    {t.name}\n                    {t.isDefault ? ' (default)' : ''}\n                  </option>\n                ))}\n              </SelectField>\n            )}\n          </div>\n        )}\n      </div>\n\n      <IconButton label=\"Preview email\" onClick={onPreview} disabled={previewing}>\n        {previewing ? <Spinner /> : <Eye size={18} strokeWidth={2} />}\n      </IconButton>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"

}

    <header\n        style={{\n          display: 'flex',\n          alignItems: 'center',\n          gap: 'var(--space-sm)',\n          padding: 'var(--space-md) var(--space-lg)',\n );\n}\n\nfunction NoEvent() {\n  return (\n    <div style={{ padding: 'var(--space-lg)' }}>\n      <Card\n        style={{\n          display: 'flex',\n          flexDirection: 'column',\n          alignItems: 'center',\n          textAlign: 'center',\n          gap: 'var(--space-sm)',\n          padding: 'var(--space-xl)',\n        }}\n      >\n        <span\n          style={{\n            display: 'inline-flex',\n            width: 48,\n            height: 48,\n            alignItems: 'center',\n            justifyContent: 'center',\n            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-pill)',\n </span>\n        <span className=\"type-title-lg\">No event open</span>\n        <span className=\"type-body text-muted\">\n          Open a Google Calendar event, then click{' '}\n          <strong>Register a visitor</strong> to issue passes for your guests.\n        </span>\n      </Card>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction LoadingState({ label }: { label: string }) {\n  return (\n    <div\n      style={{\n        flex: 1,\n        display: 'flex',\n        flexDirection: 'column',\n        alignItems: 'center',\n        justifyContent: 'center',\n        gap: 'var(--space-md)',\n </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction RosterSkeleton({ title }: { title?: string }) {\n  return (\n    <div style={{ padding: 'var(--space-lg)', display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--space-lg)' }}>\n      <Card style={{   <span className=\"type-body\">{message}</span>\n      </div>\n      <Button variant=\"tonal\" icon={<RefreshCw size={16} strokeWidth={2} />} onClick={onRetry}>\n        Try again\n      </Button>\n Phase 0 + Phase 1 are **built, committed, and green** (`tsc` clean, `wxt build` produces a loadable MV3 extension). Here's where things stand.

## What's working (code-complete)

**`auxilio-extension/`** — its own independent git repo (sibling to `auxilio-workspace`), WXT + React 19 + TS + TanStack Query + Zustand + lucide, MD3 tokens (#92288E), subtle CSS-only motion.

The full **manual-invoke flow** end-to-end against the engine's **existing** `/addon/*` contract (zero engine code changes):

- **Content script** → URL-based event detection (reads `eid`, *not* Google's DOM — robust against their UI churn) → style-isolated shadow-DOM **"Register a visitor"** button.
- **Background SW** (the only token/network holder) → `launchWebAuthFlow` mints `id_token` (engine) + `access_token` (Calendar) → `events.get` for the canonical `iCalUID`+attendees → typed `/addon/{draft,preview,send,cancel-guest}` client.
- **Side panel** → roster with per-guest include switches, blur-persisted name/phone edits, template select, **sandboxed email preview**, Send → per-guest pass results. Optimistic toggles, skeletons, honest sign-in/error states.

## To actually run it (your setup, ~10 min)

1. Create a Google **Web** OAuth client; authorized redirect `https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/`.
2. Put that client id in `auxilio-extension/.env` (`WXT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`).
3. Add the **same** client id to the engine's `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` allow-list (the only engine-side change). Then `npm run dev` → load `.output/chrome-mv3`.

## Phase 2 finding — worth your attention

I checked the engine before building the auto-nudge, and the **magic-address `.ics` auto-ingestion is retired** (engine decision D5, 2026-06-17 — `/calendar/inbound` now returns 410 unless a flag is set). The marker address still exists as `VISITOR_CALENDAR_INBOX_ADDRESS` and is still stripped from attendees.

**This doesn't break your vision — it sharpens it.** The magic address was never going to *auto-issue* passes here; it's the **intentional client-side trigger** ("only nudge when I mark the event"), which is exactly what you wanted. So Phase 2 still works: the extension detects that address among the event's attendees → auto-injects the dismissible banner (Option A). It just keys off `VISITOR_CALENDAR_INBOX_ADDRESS`, not a live auto-ingest pipeline.

All three phases are built, committed, and green. Here's the final state.

## Done — `auxilio-extension/` (independent repo, 3 commits)

| Phase | What it delivers | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **0** Scaffold | WXT + React 19 + TS + TanStack Query + Zustand + lucide; MD3 tokens (#92288E) ported from field-app; Calendar-only manifest; side-panel shell | ✅ |
| **1** Manual flow | The full registration flow your vision called for | ✅ |
| **2** Auto-nudge | Magic-address Option-A banner + live refresh | ✅ |

**The vision, mapped to what's built:**
- *Per-guest invite toggle* → MD3 switches, optimistic.
- *Edit user data* → inline name/phone (blur-persisted), template select.
- *Preview & select email template* → sandboxed iframe of the real branded email + per-guest template picker.
- *Auto-nudge when intentional* → the magic address (not every event) triggers the dismissible banner; one click opens the native side panel. Unmarked events keep a subtle "Register a visitor" button.
- *Realtime/auto-update* → a debounced observer signals the panel to refetch as guests change.
- *Quality/UX* → skeletons, honest sign-in/error states, MD3 components, subtle CSS-only motion, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected, style-isolated injected UI (shadow DOM).

**Architecture held the line:** background SW is the *only* token/network holder; content script is a dumb trigger (reads the URL `eid`, not Google's DOM); side panel is pure presentation. **Zero engine code changes** — it reuses the existing `/addon/{draft,preview,send,cancel-guest}` contract verbatim.

## Two things you should know (honest notes)

1. **Never runtime-tested in Chrome yet.** I verified statically (`tsc` clean, `wxt build` produces a loadable MV3 bundle). It needs your ~10-min setup to actually run: a Google **Web** OAuth client (redirect `https://<ext-id>.chromiumapp.org/`) → `WXT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` in `.env` → the **same** id added to the engine's `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` (the only engine-side change). Set `WXT_MAGIC_ADDRESS` to the engine's `VISITOR_CALENDAR_INBOX_ADDRESS`.

2. **"Realtime" is refetch-on-change, authoritative after Calendar save.** The engine draft is built from the Calendar API, which reflects guest changes only once the host saves. The observer keeps the panel fresh, but true *pre-save* attendee mirroring would require DOM-scraping the guest editor (fragile) — I deferred that deliberately rather than build something brittle. Flag it if you want it; it's a Phase-3 call.

## Not built (Phase 3, optional)
Sign-out control, options page (engine URL/account), toolbar badge, write-back "✓ Registered" marker onto the event, deeper a11y pass.

Want me to do the Phase 3 polish, or would you rather wire up the OAuth client and test Phases 1–2 in Chrome first? If you hit anything during testing, I can fix from the symptoms you see.

  "content": "import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';\nimport { LogOut, UserCircle2 } from 'lucide-react';\nimport { IconButton } from '@/design/components';\nimport { useAuthStatus, useSignOut } from './hooks';\n\n/** Header account control: shows the signed-in host and a sign-out action. */\nexport function AccountMenu() {\n  const auth = useAuthStatus();\n  const signOut = useSignOut();\n  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);\n  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!open) return;\n    const onDocClick = (e: MouseEvent) => {\n      if (ref.current && !ref.current.contains(e.target as Node)) setOpen(false);\n    };\n    document.addEventListener('mousedown', onDocClick);\n    return () => document.removeEventListener('mousedown', onDocClick);\n  }, [open]);\n\n  if (!auth.data?.signedIn) return null;\n\n  return (\n    <div ref={ref} style={{ position: 'relative' }}>\n      <IconButton label=\"Account\" onClick={() => setOpen((v) => !v)} aria-expanded={open}>\n        <UserCircle2 size={20} strokeWidth={2} />\n      </IconButton>\n      {open && (\n        <div\n          role=\"menu\"\n          className=\"enter\"\n          style={{\n            position: 'absolute',\n            right: 0,\n            top: '110%',\n            minWidth: 200,\n            background: 'var(--color-surface-lowest)',\n            border: '1px solid var(--color-outline-variant)',\n            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-md)',\n            boxShadow: 'var(--elev-2)',\n            padding: 'var(--space-sm)',\n            zIndex: 20,\n          }}\n        >\n          <div className=\"type-label-sm text-muted\" style={{ padding: '4px 8px 8px' }}>\n            {auth.data.email ?? 'Signed in'}\n          </div>\n          <button\n            role=\"menuitem\"\n            className=\"btn btn--text btn--block\"\n            style={{ justifyContent: 'flex-start' }}\n            disabled={signOut.isPending}\n            onClick={() => signOut.mutate(undefined, { onSuccess: () => setOpen(false) })}\n          >\n            <LogOut size={16} strokeWidth={2} />\n            {signOut.isPending ? 'Signing out…' : 'Sign out'}\n          </button>\n        </div>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

Phase 3 done, committed, green. The extension is now feature-complete across all four phases.

## Phase 3 — what I added

- **Account menu** in the panel header — signed-in email + sign out (sign-out clears the draft/resolve caches so the panel cleanly re-gates to sign-in).
- **Options page** (WXT options entrypoint) — account sign in/out, read-only engine + magic-address config, and a short "how it works."
- **Toolbar badge** on magic-address-marked events — the content script tells the background to set a badge on the icon. This is notable: it's *the exact thing we established the Calendar add-on structurally cannot do* (put a state indicator on its chrome). The extension can, so a marked event now shows a badge even before you open anything.
- **a11y pass** — `focus-visible` rings across all controls, `role="status"`/`role="alert"` live regions on the send/error banners so screen readers announce them. `prefers-reduced-motion` was already honored.

## Two things I deliberately did *not* build (flagged, not slipped in)

1. **Event write-back "✓ Registered" marker** — writing onto the Calendar event needs escalating the OAuth scope from `calendar.events.readonly` to a **write** scope. That's a sensitive-scope change to consent and the no-CASA line, so it's a conscious decision for you, not something to add silently. The in-product confirmation (pass-sent chips + success summary) covers the need without escalation.
2. **Editable engine URL in options** — our fixed `host_permissions` can't fetch arbitrary hosts, so a free-text engine URL would silently fail. Left it read-only; switching environments is a `.env` + rebuild (or a future `optional_host_permissions`).

## Where the project stands

| | |
|---|---|
| Repo | `auxilio-extension/` — own git, 4 commits (P0–P3) |
| Build | `tsc` clean, `wxt build` green; manifest has `side_panel`, `options_ui`, `action` |

Here's the complete setup checklist. There's one ordering wrinkle — the OAuth redirect URL depends on the extension's ID, so you load the extension *first*, then create the OAuth client. Do it in this order.

## Step 1 — Load the extension once to get its ID

```bash
cd auxilio-extension
npm run dev          # or: npm run build
```
- `chrome://extensions` → enable **Developer mode** → **Load unpacked** → select `.output/chrome-mv3`.
- Copy the **extension ID** shown on the card (stable for that folder path).
- Tip for the exact redirect string: click the extension's **service worker** link → in its console run `chrome.identity.getRedirectURL()`. It returns `https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/` — that's what you register in Step 2.

*(Optional: to pin the ID so it never changes, add a `key` to the manifest. Not required for single-machine dev.)*

## Step 2 — Google Cloud (reuse the existing `auxilio` project)

1. In the **same GCP project** the add-on uses, **enable the Google Calendar API** (needed for `events.get`).
2. **OAuth consent screen**: User type **Internal** (Workspace) → keeps you exempt from verification. Add scopes: `openid`, `email`, `profile`, `.../auth/calendar.events.readonly`. **Calendar-only — no Gmail/Drive** (CASA line).
3. **Credentials → Create OAuth client ID → Application type: Web application** (not "Chrome extension"). Add **Authorized redirect URI** = the `https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/` from Step 1.
4. Copy the new **Web client ID**.

## Step 3 — Engine (one env change, then restart)

In `office-ops-engine/env.updated`:
- Add the new client ID to **`AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`** (comma-separated allow-list alongside the add-on's). Without this, `/addon/*` returns 401.
- Confirm **`VISITOR_CALENDAR_INBOX_ADDRESS`** is set (the magic address). Needed only for the auto-banner/badge; the manual "Register a visitor" button works without it.
- Make sure the engine is **running and reachable** at the URL you'll point the extension to (default is the dev ingress `https://ops-engine-dev-330299.bifrost.saastack.site`), and that your test Google account is on an **internal/allowed domain** (the engine's `isInternalHostEmail` gate — use an Appointy Workspace account).

## Step 4 — Extension `.env`, then rebuild

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```
Set:
- `WXT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=<the Web client ID from Step 2>`
- `WXT_MAGIC_ADDRESS=<same value as the engine's VISITOR_CALENDAR_INBOX_ADDRESS>`
- `WXT_ENGINE_URL=` — leave default for the dev ingress, **or** point at a local/tunnel engine.

> Env is inlined at **build time**, so after editing `.env`: `npm run dev` (or `build`) again and **reload** the extension in `chrome://extensions`.

⚠️ **If you use a non-default `WXT_ENGINE_URL`** (localhost/ngrok), also add that origin to `host_permissions` in `wxt.config.ts` and rebuild — otherwise Chrome blocks the fetch (host permissions are fixed, can't fetch arbitrary hosts).

## Step 5 — First run

1. Open [Google Calendar](https://calendar.google.com), open any event.
2. Click **Register a visitor** (or the toolbar icon) → side panel opens → **Sign in with Google** (the consent window appears once).
3. Roster loads from the engine → toggle/edit/preview → **Send passes**.
4. To exercise the auto-nudge: add the magic address as a guest on an event → banner + toolbar badge should appear.

## Quick summary of what you're gathering

| Need | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Extension ID | → builds the OAuth redirect URI |
| Web OAuth client ID | → `.env` `WXT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` **and** engine `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` |
| Calendar API enabled | GCP project |
| Magic address | engine `VISITOR_CALENDAR_INBOX_ADDRESS` = `.env` `WXT_MAGIC_ADDRESS` |
| Engine up + domain gate | `office-ops-engine` running, sign in with a Workspace account |

The only piece that touches the engine is adding one client ID to an env allow-list (+ a restart). Everything else is GCP console + the extension's `.env`. If sign-in or `/addon/*` errors, the panel surfaces the real message — send me that and I'll pinpoint it.

Reusing the same `auxilio` GCP project is fine — actually the right move. Multiple OAuth client IDs coexist under one project and one consent screen with no interference. But three things to get right, because "reuse the project" has one trap:

## 1. It must be a *new* client, and a *Web application* type — you can't reuse the add-on's client id

The add-on's OAuth client is tied to its Apps Script project and is the wrong type/redirect for `launchWebAuthFlow`. So you do need to **Create OAuth client ID → Web application**, with the authorized redirect `https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/`. That gives you a **new, different** client id. Adding it doesn't touch the add-on's client at all.

## 2. The new client id MUST be added to the engine allow-list — this is the trap

The engine authorizes `/addon/*` by checking the id_token's **audience** against `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`. Right now that holds the **add-on's** client id. The extension's token will carry the **new Web client's** id as its audience — a *different* value. So:

> Add the new client id to `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` as a **comma-separated** second entry (the engine already supports a list — `addon-auth.ts:30`), then restart the engine.

"Same project" does **not** mean "same client id." If you skip this, every `/addon/*` call returns 401 even though everything else is correct. This is the single most likely thing to bite you.

## 3. No re-verification, no CASA — because it's Internal

Adding a client (and, if needed, the `calendar.events.readonly` scope) under an **Internal** consent screen triggers no verification and no CASA, since you're staying Calendar-only. The add-on is undisturbed. One cosmetic note: both surfaces share the **same consent-screen app name** — users signing into the extension see whatever the add-on's consent screen is called. Fine for internal; rename the consent screen to something neutral (e.g. "Auxilio") if you want it to read well for both.

Also make sure the **Calendar API is enabled** in the project (it should already be, since the add-on calls it).

## The one caveat that's *not* about project reuse

The extension uses the OAuth **implicit flow** (`response_type=token id_token`). Google has been tightening implicit grant on newer Web clients. If sign-in fails with a `response_type`/implicit-related error on the new client, it's a code change, not a config one — I'd switch the auth to **PKCE authorization-code flow**. Flag it if you hit it and I'll adjust `lib/auth.ts`; everything else stays the same.

**Bottom line:** reusing the project is correct and clean. Just remember the new client has a **new id** that has to land in **two** places — the extension's `.env` *and* the engine's `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` list.

Two clean answers:

## Client type: **Web application** — not Chrome extension

Create it as **Web application**. Here's why it matters for *our* code:

- The **"Chrome Extension"** OAuth client type is built for `chrome.identity.getAuthToken()`, which returns OAuth **access tokens** tied to the Chrome-signed-in profile. It doesn't cleanly give you an **id_token**, and it keys off the manifest `oauth2` block.
- Our extension uses `chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow()` with `response_type=token id_token` and the redirect `https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/`. That flow needs a client with **authorized redirect URIs** — i.e. a **Web application** client.
- And critically, the **engine verifies an id_token** (`verifyAddonIdToken` checks the token's audience). `getAuthToken` wouldn't give us that. So Web app + `launchWebAuthFlow` is what matches the existing engine contract with no change to *how* the engine authenticates.

So: **Web application**, redirect URI = `https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/`.

## New engine env var: good, but it needs a one-line engine change

Right now the engine only reads **one** audience var — `addon-auth.ts` → `audiences()` returns `process.env.AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID.split(',')`. If you put the extension's client id in a **separate** var (e.g. `AUXILIO_EXTENSION_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`), the engine won't read it until `audiences()` merges both:

```ts
function audiences(): string[] {
  return [
    ...(process.env.AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID ?? '').split(','),
    ...(process.env.AUXILIO_EXTENSION_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID ?? '').split(','),
  ].map((a) => a.trim().toLowerCase()).filter(Boolean);
}
```

So the separate-var approach is cleaner (nice separation of the two surfaces), it just turns "env-only" into "env + a one-line code change" on the engine side. Note the value is the **same** Web client id, now living in two places: the extension's `.env` (`WXT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`) and the engine's new var.

(Small heads-up: `audiences()` lowercases entries — Google client ids are case-sensitive but the numeric-`.apps.googleusercontent.com` form is already lowercase, so that's fine. I'd keep the lowercasing as-is to match the existing code.)

Want me to make that `audiences()` edit in `office-ops-engine` now? I'll add `AUXILIO_EXTENSION_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` (or whatever you want to name it) and leave a comment — no commit/deploy, just the change so it's ready when you drop the value into `env.updated`.

> DEVELOPER

do I need to add authorized URI adn redirect urls in the client?

> AGENT

For `launchWebAuthFlow`, you need **one of the two**, not both:

## Authorized redirect URIs — **YES, required**

Add exactly:
```
https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/
```
- Get the precise string by running `chrome.identity.getRedirectURL()` in the extension's service-worker console — it includes the **trailing slash**, and Google matches redirect URIs *exactly* (slash and all). A mismatch → `redirect_uri_mismatch` at sign-in.
- No domain-ownership verification needed — `chromiumapp.org` is Google's virtual domain for extensions.

## Authorized JavaScript origins — **NO, leave empty**

Those are only for the browser JS SDK / Google Identity Services running from a web page origin. `launchWebAuthFlow` doesn't use a JS origin — it round-trips through the redirect URI. You can't meaningfully register a `chrome-extension://` origin there anyway, and it's not required.

## One gotcha

The redirect URI embeds the **extension ID**. An unpacked extension's ID is stable for a given folder path, but it changes if you load from a different path or publish. If the ID changes, sign-in breaks until you add the new `https://<new-id>.chromiumapp.org/` to the client. To avoid that churn, pin the ID by adding a `key` to the manifest (I can wire that into `wxt.config.ts` if you want a fixed ID across machines/dev/published).

So: **redirect URI yes, JS origins no.**
