> DEVELOPER

all this just to auto detect event is open when a user is not oauth logged in, when we will have oauth, we won't need this way of detection, right?

> AGENT

No — that's a misconception worth correcting, because it's actually the core trade-off of the whole extension approach. OAuth and event-detection solve **two different problems**, and OAuth can't replace the detection.

## They answer different questions

| | What it does | Can the other replace it? |
|---|---|---|
| **DOM/URL detection** (`data-eventid`) | Tells us **which event the user is currently looking at**, and its id | No |
| **OAuth** (access token + id_token) | Lets us **fetch that event's details** from the Calendar API + authenticate to the engine | No |

OAuth gives you the *key to the Calendar API*, but the API has **no concept of "the event the user has open right now."** There's no endpoint for "what is junaid looking at." The only thing that knows which event is open is the **page** — so we read it from the DOM (or URL, if Google put it there, which yours doesn't). Then OAuth uses that id to fetch the authoritative details.

So the flow is: **detection gives us the event id → OAuth fetches the event by that id.** They're sequential, not alternatives. Even fully logged in, clicking an event still has to be detected the same way — the code you just tested runs identically whether you're signed in or not. Being logged out didn't cause the detection work; **Google not putting the eid in the URL** did.

## This is exactly the "DOM tax" we flagged

Remember the decision doc: the extension's permanent cost vs the add-on is **DOM coupling** — and this is precisely it. The reason the *add-on* doesn't need any of this is that Google **hands it the open event** in the `eventOpenTrigger` payload, because the add-on is a sanctioned Calendar surface. The Chrome extension is an *unsanctioned overlay*, so Google tells it nothing — the extension must infer the open event from the page itself. That inference (and keeping it working as Google reshuffles their DOM) is the standing maintenance tax we said you'd be signing up for.

## So, concretely

- This detection is **permanent**, not a logged-out workaround.
- It's the same code path before and after OAuth.
- It's the fragile bit — when Google changes `data-eventid` or their markup, this is what breaks (and the add-on is what wouldn't).

The one thing that *would* simplify it is if Google restored the `eid` in the URL — then we'd read the URL instead of the DOM (less fragile), but it'd still be "detection," still needed, still independent of OAuth.

Want me to commit the `data-eventid` detection fix now? It's the working version regardless of how the auth testing goes.

> DEVELOPER

how did the add-on able to fetch and sync with the open event, like when the event was open and I did any change, the add on was able to refresh and show me stuff.

> AGENT

Because the add-on is a **first-party Calendar surface, and Google hands it the open event directly** — through event *triggers*, not scraping. That's the whole difference.

## The mechanism: Calendar event triggers

Look at the add-on's `appsscript.json` (which I read earlier):

```json
"calendar": {
  "currentEventAccess": "READ_WRITE",
  "eventOpenTrigger":   { "runFunction": "onCalendarEventOpen" },
  "eventUpdateTrigger": { "runFunction": "onCalendarEventUpdate" }
}
```

What happens at runtime:

- **You open an event** → Google fires `eventOpenTrigger` → calls `onCalendarEventOpen(e)` and **passes the event in `e`** (the payload — attendees, organizer, title, times). The add-on reads it straight from the argument. No API call, no DOM.
- **You change the open event** (add a guest, edit) → Google fires `eventUpdateTrigger` → calls `onCalendarEventUpdate(e)` with the **updated** event. The add-on re-renders its card from the new payload. *That's* the "it refreshed and showed me stuff when I made a change."

So Google itself is pushing the event — and edits to it — into the add-on. The `currentEventAccess: READ_WRITE` + the `current.event.read/write` scopes are what make Google include the event in the payload and let the add-on write back onto it.

## Why the add-on gets this and the extension can't

| | Workspace Add-on | Chrome extension |
|---|---|---|
| Is it a registered Calendar surface? | **Yes** (Google sanctions it) | No (it's an overlay) |
| How it learns the open event | Google **hands it** in the trigger payload | Must **infer** from the DOM (`data-eventid`) |
| How it learns of edits | `eventUpdateTrigger` fires with the new event | Must **watch DOM mutations** |
| Pre-save edits visible? | **Yes** — the trigger gives the in-progress event | Hard — our engine draft is API-sourced (post-**save**) |
| Fragile to Google UI changes? | No | Yes (the DOM tax) |

This is the exact asymmetry behind everything we hit today. The add-on "just synced" because Google is a cooperative partner to it — it gets a clean, structured event object and a "the event changed" callback, for free. The extension gets **nothing** from Google about Calendar; it has to reverse-engineer "which event is open" from `data-eventid` and "something changed" from a `MutationObserver`. Same reason it can't reliably see *pre-save* edits the way the add-on can.

## The one caveat (from our earlier thread)

Even the add-on's "sync" only fires on **your** actions in the event (open/edit) — it's Google's client → add-on, never your backend → add-on. So the add-on can't be *pushed* to either; it just has a privileged, native feed of the event you're actively working on. The extension trades that privileged feed for the powers the add-on lacks (auto-open, badge, rich UI) — at the cost of the DOM gymnastics you just saw.

So: the add-on's seamless event sync is **`eventOpenTrigger` + `eventUpdateTrigger` delivering the event payload** — a sanctioned hook the Chrome extension fundamentally doesn't have, which is why we're reconstructing it from the DOM.

> DEVELOPER

we can also ask for same permissions from the user to read the calendar events.

> AGENT

We already have that permission — and it's not the missing piece. This is the crux, so let me be precise: the gap isn't *data access*, it's *UI awareness*, and no OAuth scope grants UI awareness.

## We already read calendar events

The extension holds `calendar.events.readonly`. With it we can fetch **any** event by id, list events, read attendees — all of it. That part is done. Requesting it again (or broader scopes) changes nothing, because the things we're missing aren't permissions.

## What no scope can give you

1. **"Which event is the user looking at right now."** There is no API and no permission for the user's current UI focus. The Calendar API can return event #X if you ask for #X by id — but it can't tell you the user just clicked #X on screen. That's why we still need `data-eventid` from the DOM: to learn *which* id to ask the API for.
   > Analogy: having a key to every book in the library (read scope) doesn't tell you which book the person is currently holding.

2. **Pre-save edit notifications.** The Calendar API has no real-time feed of in-progress, unsaved edits in the editor. The add-on's `eventUpdateTrigger` gives that — but it's not a scope.

## The add-on's triggers aren't permissions — and its "current event" scopes don't work in an extension

This is the key misunderstanding. `eventOpenTrigger` / `eventUpdateTrigger` are a **platform capability Google wires up only for registered Workspace Add-ons**. You can't unlock them by asking the user for an OAuth scope in a Chrome extension — extensions aren't eligible for that surface at all.

And the add-on's scopes you saw (`calendar.addons.current.event.read` / `.write`) are **add-on-runtime-only** — they govern what gets put into the *trigger payload*. Request them in a Chrome extension and they do nothing, because there's no add-on trigger context to populate a "current event." There's no add-on runtime in an extension to feed them.

## What the Calendar API *can* do for change detection (and why it's not equivalent)

- **Watch channels (push) / sync tokens** — notify a *server* when events change, at the calendar level, **after save**. That's what the engine already uses. It's not "the open event in the UI changed," and it's post-save.

So even maxed-out on scopes, we'd still:
- need the **DOM** to know which event is open, and
- only see edits **after save** (via API/watch), not the add-on's live pre-save feed.

## The honest bottom line

| Need | Source | Extension can get it? |
|---|---|---|
| Read event details by id | OAuth `calendar.events.readonly` | ✅ (have it) |
| Which event is open on screen | DOM (`data-eventid`) | ⚠️ only via DOM |
| Pushed open-event + pre-save edits | Add-on `eventOpen/UpdateTrigger` | ❌ never (add-on-only) |

Asking for the same/more permissions won't remove the DOM detection or match the add-on's live sync. That capability is a property of *being an add-on*, not of *having Calendar permissions* — which is exactly the trade we made when we chose the extension for its other powers (auto-open, badge, rich UI). The DOM detection stays; pre-save live mirroring stays hard.

> AGENT

Great question — and there's a real, useful DOM-free subset here. Let me go through each of your asks with a straight verdict, then the mechanisms.

## Verdict per feature

| What you want | Without DOM? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Reflect edits to the open event **in realtime (pre-save)** | ❌ No | No API exposes unsaved, in-editor edits. Only the DOM sees them. |
| Reflect changes **after the event is saved** | ✅ Yes | Detect the save server- or poll-side, then refetch. |
| **Notify** when a (visitor) event is saved/created | ✅ Yes | Calendar watch or polling → `chrome.notifications` + badge. |
| **Auto-open** the side panel on save | ❌ No | `sidePanel.open()` needs a *user gesture*; a push/alarm isn't one. |
| **Auto-open** when a linked event is *opened* | ❌ No (twice) | Can't detect "user opened event X" without DOM, *and* can't auto-open without a gesture. |
| Show a notification + **option to open** (user clicks) | ✅ Yes | Notify/badge with no gesture; the user's click is the gesture. |

## The two hard walls (both DOM-independent)

1. **Auto-open is impossible from any background event.** `chrome.sidePanel.open()` requires a user gesture. A Calendar watch firing, a poll finding a change, a push arriving — none are gestures. So "auto-open the extension when X happens" can never work; the best is **notify → user clicks → opens**. (Even a notification's click handler is unreliable for opening the side panel; safest is a badge/notification that nudges the user to click the icon.)
2. **"React when the user opens an event" needs the DOM.** "Opened" is a UI action; no API reports it. Only the DOM/URL knows. So the "auto-open on opening a linked invite" specifically can't be done DOM-free at all.

## What you *can* build with zero DOM

A more **passive, proactive** UX — the extension stops trying to track the open event and instead watches the calendar *as data*:

**Mechanism A — extension polls (self-contained):**
- Background `chrome.alarms` every ~1 min → Calendar API `events.list` with a **sync token** → find new/changed events → filter for the magic address (or existing invite) → `chrome.notifications.create(...)` + `chrome.action.setBadgeText`.
- No DOM, no engine dependency. Latency ≈ the poll interval (~1 min). Uses the OAuth scope you already have.

**Mechanism B — engine push (near real-time):**
- The engine already runs per-user Calendar **watch channels**; on a save it pushes via **FCM/Web Push** to the extension's service worker → notification + badge.
- Near-instant, but requires the user to have connected their calendar to the *engine* (its own OAuth/refresh token — separate from the extension's sign-in) and a push channel set up.

Both give you: *"a visitor event was just created/changed → here's a notification and a badge; click to open the panel and register."* And **post-save** changes can refresh the panel automatically (push/poll → refetch). That's all DOM-free.

## So the honest trade

A fully DOM-free extension is **possible**, but it's a **different, more passive product**:
- ✅ Notifications + badge for visitor events (saved/created).
- ✅ Panel reflects changes **after save**.
- ✅ One-click open from the nudge.
- ❌ No auto-open (ever — gesture rule).
- ❌ No live pre-save mirroring (no API for it).
- ❌ No "react the moment you open an event" (that's the DOM's job).

In other words, dropping the DOM doesn't cost you the *notification/nudge* vision — that's fully doable server/poll-side. It costs you the *in-context, as-you-edit, opens-itself-when-you-open-the-event* behaviors. Those three are exactly what the **add-on** gives natively and what the **extension** can only approximate via the DOM.

If the notification-driven, click-to-open flow is acceptable, we could even **drop the DOM detection entirely** and lean on Mechanism A (polling + alarms) — simpler, far less fragile, no maintenance tax. Want me to sketch that DOM-free variant as an option (alarms + sync-token poll + notifications + badge), so you can compare it against the current click-to-detect approach?

> AGENT

Here's the exact mechanism, straight from the add-on's code (`auxilio-workspace/Code.js`):

## 1. Two trigger functions, both just re-render the card

```js
function onCalendarEventOpen(e)   { return [buildVisitorCard_(e)]; }
function onCalendarEventUpdate(e) { return [buildVisitorCard_(e)]; }
```

These are wired in the manifest:
```json
"eventOpenTrigger":   { "runFunction": "onCalendarEventOpen" },
"eventUpdateTrigger": { "runFunction": "onCalendarEventUpdate" },
"currentEventAccess": "READ_WRITE"
```

## 2. Google *hands* the add-on the open event in `e` — including unsaved edits

Look at `loadEvent_(e)`:
```js
var cal = e.calendar || {};
var calendarId = cal.calendarId;
var eventId    = cal.id;
var payloadAtt = cal.attendees || [];          // ← the live attendee list
...
attendees: mapAttendees_(payloadAtt),          // read straight from the payload
```

`e.calendar.attendees` is the **current, in-editor attendee list** — Google populates it because the manifest declares `currentEventAccess` + the `current.event.read` scope. No DOM, no API call needed for the roster.

## 3. So the "realtime update" is this loop

1. You add/remove a guest in the open event's editor.
2. Google's Calendar client detects the change and **fires `eventUpdateTrigger`** → calls `onCalendarEventUpdate(e)`.
3. Google passes the **updated** event in `e.calendar` (the new attendee list — even before you save).
4. The function rebuilds the card from `e.calendar` and **returns it**; Google **swaps the displayed card**.

That's the whole thing. It "auto-detected and updated in realtime" because **Google pushed the changed event into the function and the function returned a fresh card.** It's event-driven by Google's client — not polling, not scraping.

(Note: it *also* calls `fetchEventWithRetry_()` — a Calendar API `events.get` — but only to fill in **saved** fields like `iCalUID`, title, and times, line 155–162. The live attendee edits come from the trigger payload, not the API. That's why guest changes show instantly while saved metadata may lag a moment.)

## Why the extension can't replicate it

| | Add-on | Extension |
|---|---|---|
| "Event changed" signal | Google **fires `eventUpdateTrigger`** | `MutationObserver` guessing |
| The changed event data | Handed in `e.calendar.attendees` (incl. unsaved) | Must scrape DOM / refetch API (saved only) |
| Re-render | Return a Card; Google swaps it | Our own React refetch |

The add-on gets a **native push of the edited event object**; the extension gets nothing from Google and must reconstruct both "it changed" (MutationObserver) and "what it is" (`data-eventid` + API). That single line — `var payloadAtt = cal.attendees` — is the capability the extension fundamentally lacks, and it's exactly why the add-on felt seamless and the extension needs the DOM gymnastics.

> DEVELOPER

okay, what can we do to reliably bring the experience as close to the add on, reliably, no temporary workarounds, a robust solution

> AGENT

Good — this is the right question to force, because "robust + closest to the add-on" actually has a hard ceiling, and pretending otherwise *is* the temporary-workaround trap. Let me give you the durable picture, then a concrete robust spec.

## The unmovable fact

The add-on's realtime in-event sync comes from **one thing no extension can obtain**: Google *pushing* the open event (incl. unsaved edits) into a trigger — `eventUpdateTrigger` + `e.calendar.attendees`. That's a platform capability exclusive to registered add-ons. **No extension engineering, no OAuth scope, conjures it.** So "robustly match the add-on" isn't an implementation problem you can out-engineer — it's an architecture choice between three honest options.

## The three robust architectures

### Option A — Hybrid: let the add-on own in-event, the extension own the rest (most robust, closest feel)
Stop making the extension *replicate* the add-on's in-event sync. Use the **add-on** for in-event registration (native realtime roster, pre-save edits, write-back — all free, all robust), and use the **extension** only for what the add-on *can't* do: auto-surface banner, toolbar badge, rich cross-event/management views, desktop power UX.
- **Robustness: highest** — the fragile part (realtime in-event) is handled by Google natively, not by you.
- **Closeness to add-on: 100%** for the in-event part, because it *is* the add-on.
- **Cost:** two surfaces, but each does only what it's good at. This is exactly the "one signal, many reactors" decision in your doc.

### Option B — Extension-primary, hardened (robust *within* the extension's limits)
If the extension must be the main in-event surface, here's the version with **no temporary workarounds** — every piece is a durable, official mechanism, and DOM reliance is contained to a single stable signal:

| Need | Robust mechanism | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Which event is open** | Read `data-eventid` on click | This is the *one* DOM dependency. It's a **semantic data attribute** Google has used for years (not a layout/CSS class) — the least-fragile DOM signal. Contain everything to it. |
| **Event details** | Calendar API `events.get` (OAuth) | Authoritative, official, you have it. |
| **Reflect changes after save** | `chrome.alarms` + Calendar API `events.list` with a **sync token**, *or* engine **watch channel → push** | Both official + durable. Sync tokens are the canonical "what changed" API. Latency ~1 min (poll) or seconds (watch). |
| **Nudge / surface** | `chrome.notifications` + `action.setBadgeText` driven by the same watch/poll | Official, robust. |
| **Graceful degradation** | If `data-eventid` ever returns nothing all session → show "open from list" fallback + log it | A Google change becomes *visible and survivable*, not a silent break. |

**Two things you must drop** (they cannot be done robustly in *any* extension):
- ❌ **Pre-save live mirroring** (reflecting edits as you type, before save) — the only source is scraping the editor's internal DOM, which is inherently fragile. Robust version = reflect **after save**.
- ❌ **Auto-open the panel** — `sidePanel.open()` requires a user gesture, period. Robust version = **notify + badge → user clicks → opens**.

So Option B ≈ the add-on **minus** (pre-save-live, auto-open) **plus** (badge, rich UI, cross-event). That's the real ceiling of a robust extension.

### Option C — Zero-DOM passive extension (most robust mechanically, furthest feel)
Drop the DOM entirely. The extension becomes a **visitor-events dashboard + nudger**: alarms+sync-token poll → notifications/badge → click to open the panel → manage from a list (not from "the open event"). No fragility at all, but it loses the in-context "on the event you're looking at" feel.

## What "robust" can and cannot include — the honest line

- ✅ Robustly doable: event identity via `data-eventid` (contained), data via Calendar API, **post-save** sync via sync tokens/watch, notify + badge.
- ❌ Not robustly doable in an extension, ever: **pre-save live edits**, **auto-open**.

Anything promising those two without the add-on is the workaround you said you don't want.

## My recommendation

**Option A (hybrid) is the genuinely robust way to get the add-on experience** — because for the in-event realtime part, you keep the add-on, which already does it natively and reliably. Make the extension the **desktop power layer** (auto-surface, badge, rich preview/manage, cross-event), and let it reflect saved state via sync tokens — not try to be a second, weaker add-on.

If leadership wants the extension as the single in-event surface, go **Option B** with eyes open: it's robust, but you consciously trade away pre-save-live and auto-open. Don't let anyone expect those — they're add-on-only.

Concretely, I'd harden the current build toward Option B by replacing the "realtime" ambition with the durable pieces: keep `data-eventid` as the sole, hardened detection signal (+ graceful fallback), and add **sync-token polling via `chrome.alarms`** for post-save refresh and **notification + badge** for the nudge. Want me to implement that — i.e. swap today's MutationObserver "live refresh" for a sync-token/alarms refresh and a notification path, and add the graceful-degradation fallback? That converts the build from "works but leans on DOM mutations" to the robust Option-B spec.

(URL `eid` is a fallback; **on current Google Calendar the URL carries no `eid`** — even the full editor uses `?state=[null,null,null,null,[N]]`.)\n- **Data:** `chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow` → Calendar API `events.get` for authoritative `iCalUID` + attendees (`auxilio-extension/lib/calendar.ts`). **Saved state only.**\n- **Change detection:** a debounced `MutationObserver` signals the side panel to refetch (`EVENT_TOUCHED`).\n- **Auth/network:** background service worker is the only token/network holder; it calls the engine's existing `/api/visitor/calendar/addon/*` contract (zero engine changes beyond an OAuth-audience env entry).\n\nNote: the engine's **magic-address `.ics` auto-ingest is retired** (D5, 2026-06-17; `/calendar/inbound` → 410 unless flagged). The marker address still exists as `VISITOR_CALENDAR_INBOX_ADDRESS` and works as the extension's **intentional client-side trigger** (banner/badge), not as an auto-issuance pipeline.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Capability matrix\n\n| Capability | Add-on | Extension | Why the difference |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Runs on Calendar **web** | ✅ | ✅ | — |\n| Runs on Calendar **mobile app** | ✅ | ❌ | Extensions are desktop-Chrome only |\n| Knows **which event is open** | ✅ (payload) | ⚠️ via DOM `data-eventid` | No API for UI focus |\n| **Pre-save** edit reflection (as you type) | ✅ (`eventUpdateTrigger`) | ❌ | No API exposes unsaved edits |\n| **Post-save** change reflection | ✅ | ✅ (sync tokens / watch) | Both official |\n| **Write back** onto the event | ✅ (`current.event.write`) | ❌ by default | Needs an OAuth write-scope escalation |\n| **Auto-open** its own UI | ❌ | ❌ | Add-on can't (anti-nag); extension can't (gesture rule) |\n| **Toolbar badge / notification** | ❌ | ✅ | Extension chrome; add-on has none |\n| **Rich UI** (free-form HTML/CSS) | ❌ (card ceiling) | ✅ | CardService vs React |\n| **Cross-event / dashboard views** | ⚠️ limited (homepage) | ✅ | — |\n| Backend can **push** to it | ❌ | ✅ (FCM/Web Push) | Add-on runs only on user action |\n| Fragile to Google UI changes | ❌ | 🔴 yes | DOM tax |\n\n---\n\n## 5. What's possible **without** the DOM\n\nOAuth/Calendar permission is already held; the gap is UI-awareness, which no scope fills.\n\n| Goal | Without DOM? | Mechanism / why not |\n|---|---|---|\n| Reflect edits **pre-save**, realtime | ❌ | No API for unsaved, in-editor edits |\n| Reflect changes **after save** | ✅ | `chrome.alarms` + Calendar API `events.list` **sync token**, or engine **watch → push** |\n| **Notify** when a (visitor) event is saved/created | ✅ | Watch/poll → `chrome.notifications` + `action.setBadgeText` |\n| **Auto-open** panel on save | ❌ | `sidePanel.open()` requires a user gesture; a push/alarm isn't one |\n| **Auto-open** when an event is *opened* | ❌ (twice) | Can't detect \"opened\" without DOM; can't auto-open without a gesture |\n| Notification + **option to open** (user clicks) | ✅ | No gesture to notify; the click is the gesture |\n\n**Two hard walls (DOM-independent):**\n1. **Auto-open is impossible from any background event** — gesture rule.\n2. **\"React when the user opens an event\" needs the DOM** — \"opened\" is a UI action no API reports.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Benefits & limitations\n\n### Workspace Add-on\n\n**Benefits**\n- **Native, robust event feed** — open event + pre-save edits handed in via triggers; no scraping, no fragility.\n- **Two-way** — write the pass link / \"✓ Registered\" onto the open event (`current.event.write`).\n- **Mobile + web** from one Apps Script codebase.\n- **₹0 infra** (Google-hosted), admin one-click domain install, no DOM-maintenance tax.\n- **Internal-first**, Calendar-only → no OAuth verification, no CASA.\n\n**Limitations**\n- **Card ceiling** — compose only from the CardService widget catalog; every interaction is a server round-trip that rebuilds a card; fragile multi-field form state; limited rich text (the documented D5 risk).\n- **Cannot auto-open or badge** — no attention-grab; the user must open the side panel.\n- **No backend push** — runs only on the user's open/edit/action; the engine can't poke it.\n- **Apps Script runtime** — V8, no npm/TS build, logs-in-editor debugging.\n\n### Chrome Extension\n\n**Benefits**\n- **Rich UI** — full React/HTML/CSS; smooth toggles, real email preview, inline edits (escapes the card ceiling).\n- **Can grab attention** — toolbar **badge** + **notifications**; the intentional auto-**banner** (Option A) — things the add-on structurally can't do.\n- **Backend-pushable** — FCM/Web Push for near-real-time nudges; cross-event/dashboard views.\n- **Owns its stack** — WXT + React + our MD3 tokens.\n\n**Limitations**\n- **Desktop Chrome only** — no mobile, no Calendar mobile app.\n- **DOM-coupling tax** — identity (`data-eventid`) and change-detection (MutationObserver) ride on Google's markup; a Google change can break them. Mitigated by depending on the single **semantic `data-eventid` attribute** (not layout/CSS) + graceful degradation, but never zero-risk.\n- **No pre-save live edits** — only saved state (API).\n- **No auto-open** — gesture rule; best is notify → click → open.\n- **Write-back needs scope escalation** — `calendar.events.readonly` → a write scope (a deliberate, sensitive-scope decision).\n- **Two Google dependencies** for public/commercial — Chrome Web Store review *and* OAuth verification (still no CASA if Calendar-only).\n\n---\n\n## 7. The robust architecture options (no temporary workarounds)\n\n### Option A — Hybrid (most robust, closest to the add-on feel) — **recommended**\nAdd-on owns **in-event** (native realtime roster, pre-save edits, write-back); extension owns the **complement** (auto-surface banner, badge, rich preview/manage, cross-event, desktop power UX). The fragile/in-context realtime part is handled by Google natively — nothing brittle required for it. Matches the \"one signal (magic address), many reactors\" model.\n\n### Option B — Extension-primary, hardened (robust within the extension's limits)\n- **Identity:** `data-eventid` on click — the *single*, most-stable DOM signal; contain everything to it + graceful fallback (\"open from list\" + log) if it ever disappears.\n- **Data:** Calendar API `events.get` (authoritative, official).\n- **Post-save refresh:** `chrome.alarms` + Calendar API **sync token**, or engine **watch → push**.\n- **Nudge:** `chrome.notifications` + `action.setBadgeText`.\n- **Consciously dropped (not robustly achievable in any extension):** pre-save live mirroring, auto-open. Result ≈ add-on **minus** those two **plus** badge/rich-UI/cross-event.\n\n### Option C — Zero-DOM passive (most robust mechanically, furthest feel)\nNo DOM at all: alarms + sync-token poll → notifications/badge → click to open → manage from a list (not \"the open event\"). Zero fragility, but loses the in-context feel.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Recommendation\n\n- **For the full add-on experience, robustly: Option A (hybrid).** Don't make the extension a weaker second add-on; let the add-on do the in-event realtime it does natively, and let the extension do what only it can (badge, rich UI, cross-event, push nudges).\n- **If the extension must be the single in-event surface: Option B**, with eyes open that **pre-save-live and auto-open are add-on-only** and are dropped. Replace today's MutationObserver \"live refresh\" with **sync-token polling (`chrome.alarms`)** for post-save refresh + **notification/badge**, and keep `data-eventid` as the one hardened detection signal with graceful degradation.\n- **Never promise** auto-open or pre-save-live in an extension — that's the workaround trap.\n\n---\n\n## 9. References (code)\n- Add-on triggers: `auxilio-workspace/appsscript.json`, `auxilio-workspace/Code.js` (`onCalendarEventOpen/Update`, `loadEvent_`).\n- Extension detection/data: `auxilio-extension/entrypoints/calendar.content.ts`, `auxilio-extension/lib/calendar.ts`, `lib/engine.ts`, `entrypoints/background.ts`.\n- Engine contract: `office-ops-engine/spec/2026-06-16_calendar_addon_register_endpoint.md`; magic-address retirement: `office-ops-engine/src/mastra/modules/visitor/routes.ts:504`, `calendar-ingest.ts:81`.\n"
}

lets go for option B, but keep in mind, we may move to option A if option B does not suffice the need.   Option B — Extension-primary, hardened (robust within the extension's limits)

  If the extension must be the main in-event surface, here's the version with no temporary workarounds — every piece is a durable, official mechanism, and DOM reliance is
  contained to a single stable signal:

  ┌────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │        Need        │                    Robust mechanism                    │                                           Notes                                            │
  ├────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Which event is     │ Read data-eventid on click                             │ This is the one DOM dependency. It's a semantic data attribute Google has used for years   │
  │ open               │                                                        │ (not a layout/CSS class) — the least-fragile DOM signal. Contain everything to it.         │
  ├────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Event details      │ Calendar API events.get (OAuth)                        │ Authoritative, official, you have it.                                                      │
  ├────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Reflect changes    │ chrome.alarms + Calendar API events.list with a sync   │ Both official + durable. Sync tokens are the canonical "what changed" API. Latency ~1 min  │
  │ after save         │ token, or engine watch channel → push                  │ (poll) or seconds (watch).                                                                 │
  ├────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Nudge / surface    │ chrome.notifications + action.setBadgeText driven by   │ Official, robust.                                                                          │
  │                    │ the same watch/poll                                    │                                                                                            │
  ├────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Graceful           │ If data-eventid ever returns nothing all session →     │ A Google change becomes visible and survivable, not a silent break.                        │
  │ degradation        │ show "open from list" fallback + log it                │                                                                                            │
  └────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Two things you must drop (they cannot be done robustly in any extension):
  - ❌ Pre-save live mirroring (reflecting edits as you type, before save) — the only source is scraping the editor's internal DOM, which is inherently fragile. Robust version =
  reflect after save.
  - ❌ Auto-open the panel — sidePanel.open() requires a user gesture, period. Robust version = notify + badge → user clicks → opens.

  So Option B ≈ the add-on minus (pre-save-live, auto-open) plus (badge, rich UI, cross-event). That's the real ceiling of a robust extension.

{

  "content": "/**\n * Calendar read (background only). Two jobs:\n *  1) resolve the canonical event for a given eid (events.get) — authoritative\n *     iCalUID + attendees for the side panel.\n *  2) list changes via a sync token (events.list) — the durable \"what changed\"\n *     API that drives post-save refresh + the visitor-event nudge/badge.\n * Calendar.events.readonly only.\n */\nimport { MAGIC_ADDRESS } from './config';\nimport type { ActiveEvent } from './types';\n\n/** `eid` is URL-safe base64 of \"<eventId> <calendarId>\" (calendarId optional). */\nexport function decodeEid(eid: string): { eventId: string; calendarId: string } | null {\n  try {\n    let b64 = eid.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');\n    b64 += '='.repeat((4 - (b64.length % 4)) % 4);\n    const decoded = atob(b64);\n    const [eventId, calendarId] = decoded.split(' ');\n    if (!eventId) return null;\n    return { eventId, calendarId: calendarId || 'primary' };\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Inverse of decodeEid — build an eid the side panel can resolve. */\nexport function encodeEid(eventId: string, calendarId = 'primary'): string {\n  const b64 = btoa(`${eventId} ${calendarId}`);\n  return b64.replace(/\\+/g, '-').replace(/\\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, '');\n}\n\nexport interface GCalEvent {\n  id?: string;\n  iCalUID?: string;\n  status?: string;\n  summary?: string;\n  location?: string;\n  start?: { dateTime?: string; date?: string };\n  end?: { dateTime?: string; date?: string };\n  organizer?: { email?: string };\n  attendees?: {\n    email?: string;\n    displayName?: string;\n    resource?: boolean;\n    self?: boolean;\n    organizer?: boolean;\n  }[];\n}\n\n/** Is this a visitor event? (magic address among attendees or in the location.) */\nexport function isMarked(ev: GCalEvent): boolean {\n  if (!MAGIC_ADDRESS) return false;\n  const inAttendees = (ev.attendees ?? []).some(\n    (a) => a.email?.toLowerCase() === MAGIC_ADDRESS,\n  );\n  const inLocation = (ev.location ?? '').toLowerCase().includes(MAGIC_ADDRESS);\n  return inAttendees || inLocation;\n}\n\nfunction startOf(ev: GCalEvent): string | undefined {\n  return ev.start?.dateTime ?? ev.start?.date;\n}\n\nexport async function fetchActiveEvent(\n  eid: string,\n  accessToken: string,\n): Promise<ActiveEvent> {\n  const dec = decodeEid(eid);\n  if (!dec) throw new Error('Could not read the event id from this page.');\n\n  const url = new URL(\n    `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/${encodeURIComponent(\n      dec.calendarId,\n    )}/events/${encodeURIComponent(dec.eventId)}`,\n  );\n  url.searchParams.set(\n    'fields',\n    'iCalUID,summary,location,start,end,organizer,attendees(email,displayName,resource,self,organizer)',\n  );\n\n  const res = await fetch(url, {\n    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },\n  });\n  if (!res.ok) {\n    if (res.status === 404) throw new Error('This event was not found on your calendar.');\n    throw new Error(`Calendar API error (${res.status}).`);\n  }\n  const ev = (await res.json()) as GCalEvent;\n\n  const attendees = (ev.attendees ?? [])\n    .filter((a) => a.email && !a.resource && a.email.toLowerCase() !== MAGIC_ADDRESS)\n    .map((a) => ({ email: a.email as string, name: a.displayName }));\n\n  return {\n    iCalUid: ev.iCalUID ?? '',\n    providerEventId: dec.eventId,\n    title: ev.summary,\n    start: startOf(ev),\n    end: ev.end?.dateTime ?? ev.end?.date,\n    location: ev.location,\n    organizerEmail: ev.organizer?.email,\n    attendees,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * List changes on the primary calendar. With a sync token → only what changed\n * since last sync; without → an initial window of upcoming events (and a fresh\n * token). Paginates to capture nextSyncToken. Returns expired:true on a 410 so\n * the caller can full-resync.\n */\nexport async function listEvents(\n  accessToken: string,\n  opts: { syncToken?: string } = {},\n): Promise<{ items: GCalEvent[]; nextSyncToken?: string; expired?: boolean }> {\n  const items: GCalEvent[] = [];\n  let pageToken: string | undefined;\n  let nextSyncToken: string | undefined;\n\n  do {\n    const url = new URL(\n      'https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/primary/events',\n    );\n    url.searchParams.set('singleEvents', 'true');\n    url.searchParams.set('showDeleted', 'true');\n    url.searchParams.set('maxResults', '250');\n    url.searchParams.set(\n      'fields',\n      'items(id,iCalUID,status,summary,location,start,end,attendees(email,resource)),nextPageToken,nextSyncToken',\n    );\n    if (opts.syncToken) {\n      url.searchParams.set('syncToken', opts.syncToken);\n    } else {\n      // Initial sync: a forward window keeps the token small and relevant.\n      url.searchParams.set('timeMin', new Date().toISOString());\n    }\n    if (pageToken) url.searchParams.set('pageToken', pageToken);\n\n    const res = await fetch(url, {\n      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },\n    });\n    if (res.status === 410) return { items: [], expired: true }; // sync token stale\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Calendar list error (${res.status}).`);\n    const data = (await res.json()) as {\n      items?: GCalEvent[];\n      nextPageToken?: string;\n      nextSyncToken?: string;\n    };\n    if (data.items) items.push(...data.items);\n    pageToken = data.nextPageToken;\n    nextSyncToken = data.nextSyncToken ?? nextSyncToken;\n  } while (pageToken);\n\n  return { items, nextSyncToken };\n}\n"
}

The durable, official \"what changed\" engine:\n * runs on a chrome.alarm, lists changes via a sync token, and maintains the set\n * of upcoming visitor (magic-address) events in storage.local. Drives:\n *  - post-save refresh of the open event (changedIds),\n *  - the visitor-event notification + toolbar badge (newMarked / count),\n *  - the side panel's \"open from list\" picker (listMarked).\n * No DOM. Reflects SAVED state only (pre-save edits are add-on-only — see\n * Planning-docs/2026-06-19_calendar_addon_vs_extension_capabilities.md).\n */\nimport { encodeEid, isMarked, listEvents } from './calendar';\nimport type { VisitorEventSummary } from './types';\n\nconst SYNC_TOKEN_KEY = 'auxilio.syncToken';\nconst MARKED_KEY = 'auxilio.markedEvents';\nconst PAST_GRACE_MS = 60 * 60_000; // keep events until 1h after they end\n\ntype MarkedMap = Record<string, VisitorEventSummary>;\n\nasync function readMarked(): Promise<MarkedMap> {\n  const r = await chrome.storage.local.get(MARKED_KEY);\n  return (r[MARKED_KEY] as MarkedMap) ?? {};\n}\n\nexport interface SyncResult {\n  changedIds: Set<string>;\n  newMarked: VisitorEventSummary[];\n  markedCount: number;\n}\n\n/** Pull changes since the last sync; update the marked set; report deltas. */\nexport async function runSync(accessToken: string): Promise<SyncResult> {\n  const store = await chrome.storage.local.get([SYNC_TOKEN_KEY, MARKED_KEY]);\n  let syncToken = store[SYNC_TOKEN_KEY] as string | undefined;\n  let marked = (store[MARKED_KEY] as MarkedMap) ?? {};\n\n  let resp = await listEvents(accessToken, { syncToken });\n  if (resp.expired) {\n    // Token stale → full resync from scratch.\n    syncToken = undefined;\n    marked = {};\n    resp = await listEvents(accessToken, {});\n  }\n\n  const changedIds = new Set<string>();\n  const newMarked: VisitorEventSummary[] = [];\n\n  for (const ev of resp.items) {\n    if (!ev.id) continue;\n    changedIds.add(ev.id);\n    const cancelled = ev.status === 'cancelled';\n    if (isMarked(ev) && !cancelled) {\n      const summary: VisitorEventSummary = {\n        eid: encodeEid(ev.id, 'primary'),\n        eventId: ev.id,\n        iCalUid: ev.iCalUID ?? '',\n        title: ev.summary || '(no title)',\n        start: ev.start?.dateTime ?? ev.start?.date,\n      };\n      if (!marked[ev.id]) newMarked.push(summary);\n      marked[ev.id] = summary;\n    } else {\n      delete marked[ev.id]; // unmarked or cancelled\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Prune events that are well past.\n  const cutoff = Date.now() - PAST_GRACE_MS;\n  for (const id of Object.keys(marked)) {\n    const s = marked[id].start;\n    if (s && Date.parse(s) < cutoff) delete marked[id];\n  }\n\n  await chrome.storage.local.set({\n    [SYNC_TOKEN_KEY]: resp.nextSyncToken ?? syncToken,\n    [MARKED_KEY]: marked,\n  });\n\n  return { changedIds, newMarked, markedCount: Object.keys(marked).length };\n}\n\n/** Upcoming visitor events, soonest first — for the panel's picker. */\nexport async function listMarked(): Promise<VisitorEventSummary[]> {\n  const marked = await readMarked();\n  return Object.values(marked).sort((a, b) =>\n    (a.start ?? '').localeCompare(b.start ?? ''),\n  );\n}\n\n/** Is this event id currently a known visitor event? */\nexport async function isEventMarked(eventId: string): Promise<boolean> {\n  const marked = await readMarked();\n  return !!marked[eventId];\n}\n"
}

// broadcasts\n    handle(msg, sender)\n      .then(sendResponse)\n      .catch((err) => sendResponse(fail(err)));\n    return true; // async response\n  });\n\n  console.log('[auxilio] background ready');\n});\n\n// ─────────────────────────── sync loop ───────────────────────────\n\nasync function doSync(): Promise<void> {\n  let accessToken: string;\n  try {\n    accessToken = (await getValidTokens()).accessToken;\n  } catch {\n    return; // not signed in — nothing to poll\n  }\n  let result;\n  try {\n    result = await runSync(accessToken);\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.warn('[auxilio] sync failed', err);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // Toolbar badge = number of upcoming visitor events (the on-icon nudge).\n  await chrome.action.setBadgeBackgroundColor({ color: BADGE_COLOR });\n  await chrome.action.setBadgeText({\n    text: result.markedCount > 0 ? String(result.markedCount) : '',\n  });\n\n  // OS notification for each newly-discovered visitor event.\n  for (const ev of result.newMarked) notifyVisitorEvent(ev);\n\n  // If the event the panel is showing changed (post-save), tell it to refetch.\n  const stored = await chrome.storage.session.get(ACTIVE_EID_KEY);\n  const activeEid = stored[ACTIVE_EID_KEY] as string | undefined;\n  if (activeEid) {\n    const dec = decodeEid(activeEid);\n    if (dec && result.changedIds.has(dec.eventId)) broadcastRefreshActive();\n  }\n}\n\nfunction notifyVisitorEvent(ev: VisitorEventSummary): void {\n  chrome.notifications.create(`auxilio:${ev.eventId}`, {\n    type: 'basic',\n    iconUrl: chrome.runtime.getURL('icon/128.png'),\n    title: 'Visitor event',\n    message: `${ev.title} — open Auxilio to register passes`,\n    priority: 1,\n  });\n}\n\n// ─────────────────────────── RPC plumbing ───────────────────────────\n\nconst ok = <T,>(data: T): RpcResponse<T> => ({ ok: true, data });\n\nfunction fail(err: unknown): RpcResponse<never> {\n  const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n  const status = err instanceof EngineError ? err.status : undefined;\n  return { ok: false, error: message, status, needsAuth: status === 401 };\n}\n\nasync function withTokens<T>(\n  fn: (t: { idToken: string; accessToken: string }) => Promise<T>,\n): Promise<RpcResponse<T>> {\n  let tokens;\n  try {\n    tokens = await getValidTokens();\n  } catch {\n    return { ok: false, error: 'Sign in to continue.', needsAuth: true };\n  }\n  try {\n    return ok(await fn(tokens));\n  } catch (err) {\n    return fail(err);\n  }\n}\n\nconst withIdToken = <T,>(fn: (idToken: string) => Promise<T>) =>\n  withTokens((t) => fn(t.idToken));\n\nasync function handle(\n  msg: RpcRequest,\n  sender: chrome.runtime.MessageSender,\n): Promise<RpcResponse<unknown>> {\n  switch (msg.type) {\n    case 'AUTH_STATUS':\n      return ok(await authStatus());\n    case 'AUTH_SIGN_IN': {\n      const status = await signIn();\n      void doSync(); // warm the marked set + badge right after sign-in\n      return ok(status);\n    }\n    case 'AUTH_SIGN_OUT':\n      await signOut();\n      await chrome.action.setBadgeText({ text: '' });\n      return ok({ signedIn: false });\n\n    case 'OPEN_FOR_EVENT': {\n      await chrome.storage.session.set({ [ACTIVE_EID_KEY]: msg.eid });\n      let opened = false;\n      try {\n        const tabId = sender.tab?.id;\n        if (tabId != null) {\n          await chrome.sidePanel.open({ tabId });\n          opened = true;\n        }\n      } catch {\n        // Gesture may not have carried; the user can click the toolbar icon.\n      }\n      return ok({ opened });\n    }\n\n    case 'RESOLVE_EVENT':\n      return withTokens((t) => fetchActiveEvent(msg.eid, t.accessToken));\n\n    case 'DRAFT_LOAD':\n      return withIdToken((t) => engine.loadDraft(t, msg.event));\n    case 'DRAFT_PATCH':\n      return withIdToken((t) => engine.patchDraft(t, msg.iCalUid, msg.patch));\n    case 'PREVIEW':\n      return withIdToken((t) => engine.preview(t, msg.iCalUid, msg.visitorEmail));\n    case 'SEND':\n      return withIdToken((t) => engine.send(t, msg.iCalUid, msg.start, msg.end));\n    case 'CANCEL_GUEST':\n      return withIdToken((t) =>\n        engine.cancelGuest(t, msg.iCalUid, msg.invitationId),\n      );\n\n    case 'LIST_VISITOR_EVENTS':\n      return withTokens(async (t) => {\n        await runSync(t.accessToken);   "content": "/**\n * Content script on Google Calendar — the ONE contained DOM dependency.\n *\n * Robustness contract (Option B): the only thing we read from Google's DOM is\n * the `data-eventid` attribute on a clicked event chip — a long-standing\n * *semantic* attribute (base64url of \"<eventId> <calendarId>\"), not a layout/CSS\n * class. If `data-eventid`\n * ever disappears, we log it and the side panel's \"open from list\" fallback\n * still works.\n */\nexport default defineContentScript({\n  matches: ['https://calendar.google.com/*'],\n  main() {\n    let eid: string | null = null;\n    let everSawEventId = false;\n\n    const fab = mountFab((e) => openFor(e));\n\n    function setEid(next: string | null) {\n      if (next === eid) return;\n      eid = next;\n      fab.setEid(eid);\n    }\n\n    // Primary trigger: the clicked event chip carries the event id as\n    // `data-eventid`. Works for the popover, where the URL has no eid.\n    document.addEventListener(\n      'click',\n      (e) => {\n        const chip = (e.target as Element | null)?.closest?.('[data-eventid]');\n        const id = chip?.getAttribute('data-eventid');\n        if (id) {\n          everSawEventId = true;\n          setEid(id);\n        }\n      },\n      true,\n    );\n\n    // Escape closes the popover/editor → drop the active event.\n    document.addEventListener(\n      'keydown',\n      (e) => {\n        if (e.key === 'Escape') setEid(null);\n      },\n      true,\n    );\n\n    // Fallback: some Calendars still expose the eid in the URL.\n    let lastUrlEid: string | null = null;\n    setInterval(() => {\n      const u = currentEid();\n      if (u && u !== lastUrlEid) {\n        lastUrlEid = u;\n        setEid(u);\n      }\n    }, 1000);\n    window.addEventListener('popstate', () => {\n      const u = currentEid();\n      if (u) setEid(u);\n    });\n\n    // Graceful-degradation telemetry: if Google ever drops `data-eventid`, this\n    // surfaces it instead of failing silently. The panel's list view still works.\n    setTimeout(() => {\n      if (!everSawEventId && !document.querySelector('[data-eventid]')) {\n        console.warn(\n          '[auxilio] no [data-eventid] found — click detection may be unavailable; use the panel’s event list.',\n        );\n      }\n    }, 90_000);\n\n    console.log('[auxilio] content script ready on Google Calendar');\n  },\n});\n\nfunction openFor(eid: string) {\n  return chrome.runtime\n    .sendMessage({ type: 'OPEN_FOR_EVENT', eid })\n    .catch((err) => console.error('[auxilio] open failed', err));\n}\n\n/** Fallback only: extract the event id from the URL, if present. */\nfunction currentEid(): string | null {\n  const path = location.pathname.match(/\\/eventedit\\/([^/?#]+)/);\n  if (path && path[1] !== 'eventedit') return safeDecode(path[1]);\n  const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('eid');\n  return q ? safeDecode(q) : null;\n}\n\nfunction safeDecode(s: string): string {\n  try {\n    return decodeURIComponent(s);\n  } catch {\n    return s;\n  }\n}\n\nconst USER_PLUS_SVG = `\n<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"20\" height=\"20\" viewBox=\"0 0 24 24\"\n  fill=\"none\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"2.2\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\">\n  <path d=\"M16 21v-2a4 4 0 0 0-4-4H6a4 4 0 0 0-4 4v2\"/><circle cx=\"9\" cy=\"7\" r=\"4\"/>\n  <line x1=\"19\" x2=\"19\" y1=\"8\" y2=\"14\"/><line x1=\"22\" x2=\"16\" y1=\"11\" y2=\"11\"/></svg>`;\n\n/** Floating \"Register a visitor\" button, shown for the clicked event. */\nfunction mountFab(onClick: (eid: string) => void) {\n  const host = document.createElement('div');\n  host.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;right:24px;bottom:24px;z-index:2147483646;';\n  document.documentElement.appendChild(host);\n  const root = host.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });\n  root.innerHTML = `\n    <style>\n      :host { all: initial; }\n      .fab {\n        display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;\n        font-family:'Google Sans','Roboto',system-ui,sans-serif;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;\n        color:#fff;background:#92288e;border:none;border-radius:999px;padding:12px 18px;\n        box-shadow:0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.18);cursor:pointer;\n        transform:translateY(8px);opacity:0;pointer-events:none;\n        transition:opacity 200ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1),transform 200ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1),box-shadow 120ms ease;\n      }\n      .fab.show{opacity:1;transform:none;pointer-events:auto;}\n      .fab:hover{box-shadow:0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.24);}\n      .fab:active{transform:scale(.98);}\n      .fab[disabled]{opacity:.6;pointer-events:none;}\n      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.fab{transition:none;transform:none;}}\n    </style>\n    <button class=\"fab\" type=\"button\">${USER_PLUS_SVG}<span class=\"label\">Register a visitor</span></button>`;\n  const btn = root.querySelector('button') as HTMLButtonElement;\n  const label = root.querySelector('.label') as HTMLSpanElement;\n  let current: string | null = null;\n  btn.addEventListener('click', async () => {\n    if (!current) return;\n    btn.disabled = true;\n    label.textContent = 'Opening…';\n    try {\n      await onClick(current);\n    } finally {\n      btn.disabled = false;\n      label.textContent = 'Register a visitor';\n    }\n  });\n  return {\n    setEid(next: string | null) {\n      current = next;\n      btn.classList.toggle('show', !!next);\n    },\n  };\n}\n"

  "content": "import { CalendarClock, ChevronRight, UserPlus } from 'lucide-react';\nimport { Card, Spinner } from '@/design/components';\nimport type { AuthStatus, VisitorEventSummary } from '@/lib/types';\nimport { SignInGate } from './SignInGate';\n\n/**\n * Shown when no event is active. Doubles as the \"open from list\" fallback if\n * click-detection ever breaks: pick an upcoming visitor event to register.\n * Signed-out users get the sign-in here too (no need to open an event first).\n */\nexport function EmptyState({\n  auth,\n  events,\n  loading,\n  onPick,\n}: {\n  auth: AuthStatus | undefined;\n  events: VisitorEventSummary[] | undefined;\n  loading: boolean;\n  onPick: (eid: string) => void;\n}) {\n  if (!auth) {\n    return (\n      <Centered>\n        <Spinner size={22} />\n      </Centered>\n    );\n  }\n  if (!auth.signedIn) {\n    return <SignInGate reason=\"Sign in to see your visitor events and register passes.\" />;\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div style={{ padding: 'var(--space-lg)', display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--space-lg)' }}>\n      <Card\n        style={{\n          display: 'flex',\n          alignItems: 'center',\n          gap: 'var(--space-md)',\n          padding: 'var(--space-lg)',\n        }}\n      >\n        <span\n          style={{\n            display: 'inline-flex',\n            width: 40,\n            height: 40,\n            flex: '0 0 auto',\n            alignItems: 'center',\n            justifyContent: 'center',\n            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-pill)',\n            background: 'var(--color-primary-container)',\n            color: 'var(--color-on-primary-container)',\n          }}\n        >\n          <UserPlus size={20} strokeWidth={2} />\n        </span>\n        <span className=\"type-body text-muted\">\n          Open a Calendar event and click <strong>Register a visitor</strong>, or pick\n          a visitor event below.\n        </span>\n      </Card>\n\n      <section>\n        <div\n          className=\"type-label-sm text-muted\"\n          style={{ textTransform: 'uppercase', marginBottom: 4 }}\n        >\n          Upcoming visitor events\n        </div>\n\n        {loading && !events ? (\n          <Centered>\n            <Spinner size={20} />\n          </Centered>\n        ) : events && events.length > 0 ? (\n          <Card style={{ paddingTop: 0, paddingBottom: 0 }}>\n            {events.map((ev) => (\n              <button\n                key={ev.eid}\n                className=\"row\"\n                onClick={() => onPick(ev.eid)}\n                style={{\n                  width: '100%',\n                  background: 'transparent',\n                  border: 'none',\n                  font: 'inherit',\n                  textAlign: 'left',\n                  cursor: 'pointer',\n                }}\n              >\n                <CalendarClock\n                  size={18}\n                  strokeWidth={2}\n                  style={{ flex: '0 0 auto', color: 'var(--color-on-surface-variant)' }}\n                />\n                <div className=\"row__grow\">\n                  <div className=\"type-label row__ellipsis\">{ev.title}</div>\n                  {ev.start && (\n                    <div className=\"type-label-sm text-muted\">{formatWhen(ev.start)}</div>\n                  )}\n                </div>\n                <ChevronRight\n                  size={18}\n                  strokeWidth={2}\n                  style={{ flex: '0 0 auto', color: 'var(--color-outline)' }}\n                />\n              </button>\n            ))}\n          </Card>\n        ) : (\n          <Card className=\"type-body text-muted\">\n            No upcoming visitor events found. They appear here once an event includes\n            the visitor address.\n          </Card>\n        )}\n      </section>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction Centered({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {\n  return (\n    <div\n      style={{\n        display: 'flex',\n        alignItems: 'center',\n        justifyContent: 'center',\n        padding: 'var(--space-xxl)',\n        color: 'var(--color-on-surface-variant)',\n      }}\n    >\n      {children}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction formatWhen(start: string): string {\n  const allDay = !start.includes('T');\n  const d = new Date(start);\n  const date = d.toLocaleDateString(undefined, { weekday: 'short', day: 'numeric', month: 'short' });\n  if (allDay) return `${date} · All day`;\n  return `${date} · ${d.toLocaleTimeString(undefined, { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' })}`;\n}\n"
}

## What changed (the durable architecture)

**DOM reliance is now contained to one signal** — `data-eventid` on click → the "Register a visitor" FAB. Everything fragile is gone:
- ❌ removed: magic-address DOM text-scan, in-page banner, `MutationObserver` "live refresh", content-driven badge.

**Change detection is now the official "what changed" API** (`lib/calendar-sync.ts`):
- Background polls Calendar `events.list` with a **sync token** on a `chrome.alarms` (~1 min).
- Maintains the set of upcoming **visitor events** → fires `chrome.notifications` + sets the **toolbar badge** for new ones, and broadcasts `REFRESH_ACTIVE` so the open event **refetches after save**.

**Open-from-list empty state** (`EmptyState.tsx`):
- Signed out → sign in *right here* (fixes the earlier gap where the empty panel had no sign-in).
- Signed in → pick from your upcoming visitor events (`LIST_VISITOR_EVENTS`).
- This is also the **graceful fallback**: if click-detection ever breaks, the list still works.

**Consciously not built** (add-on-only, can't be robust in any extension, per your decision): pre-save live mirroring and auto-open. The extension reflects **saved state only**.

> AGENT

Found it — and it's a quick fix. You pasted the **client *secret*** into `WXT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, not the client **ID**.

The masked value shows `GOCSPX…` — that's the format of a Google OAuth **client secret**. A client **ID** looks like:
```
123456789012-abcdefg....apps.googleusercontent.com
```
So Google received a "client_id" that's actually a secret → "OAuth client was not found / invalid_client." (The build pipeline is fine — your value *was* inlined; it's just the wrong value.)

## Fix

1. In Google Cloud → your OAuth client → copy the field labeled **"Client ID"** (ends in `.apps.googleusercontent.com`), **not** "Client secret."
2. In `auxilio-extension/.env`:
   ```
   WXT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=123456789012-xxxxxxxx.apps.googleusercontent.com
   ```
3. Rebuild + reload:
   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```
   then hit **reload** on the extension card in `chrome://extensions`.

## Two important notes

- **Don't put the client secret in the extension at all.** Our flow (`launchWebAuthFlow`, implicit) only needs the public **client ID** — the secret is never used and must not ship in a browser extension. Drop it from `.env`.
- **The secret got inlined into your local `.output/` build** (gitignored, not committed, local only). It's not exposed publicly, but since it's a real credential you no longer need, the clean move is to **rotate that client secret** in Google Cloud when convenient. Not urgent, just hygiene.
- **Check the engine too:** `AUXILIO_EXTENSION_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` in `env.updated` must also be the **client ID** (the `.apps.googleusercontent.com` value), not the secret — otherwise `/addon/*` will reject the token even after sign-in works.

Swap in the client ID, rebuild, and the consent screen should load. If it then errors on `redirect_uri_mismatch`, that's the next thing (the `chromiumapp.org` redirect) — but invalid_client is purely the wrong client value.

In order of likelihood:

- **Client doesn't exist in the expected project / wrong type.** In Google Cloud Console → **APIs & Services → Credentials**, confirm:
  - a client with id `561888594292-…` exists, and

  - it's in the **same project** whose OAuth consent screen you configured (Internal). The numeric prefix `561888594292` is that project's number — make sure the consent screen lives in that project.
- **No OAuth consent screen configured** in that project → also blocks; configure it (User type Internal).

## Issue 1: FAB doesn't open the panel — a gesture-ordering bug

`chrome.sidePanel.open()` requires a live user gesture, and our handler does `await chrome.storage.session.set(...)` **before** calling `open()` — that `await` consumes the gesture, so `open()` silently fails. Fix: call `open()` first (synchronously), then store. Let me also stop swallowing the error so we can see it if it still fails.

  "old_string": "    case 'OPEN_FOR_EVENT': {\n      await chrome.storage.session.set({ [ACTIVE_EID_KEY]: msg.eid });\n      let opened = false;\n      try {\n        const tabId = sender.tab?.id;\n        if (tabId != null) {\n          await chrome.sidePanel.open({ tabId });\n          opened = true;\n        }\n      } catch {\n        // Gesture may not have carried; the user can click the toolbar icon.\n      }\n      return ok({ opened });\n    }",
  "new_string": "    case 'OPEN_FOR_EVENT': {\n      // Open the panel FIRST, before any await, so the content-script click's\n      // user activation is still valid — sidePanel.open() requires a gesture.\n      const tabId = sender.tab?.id;\n      let opened = false;\n      if (tabId != null) {\n        try {\n          await chrome.sidePanel.open({ tabId });\n          opened = true;\n        } catch (err) {\n          console.warn('[auxilio] sidePanel.open failed (gesture not carried?)', err);\n        }\n      }\n      // Store after — the panel reacts to this via storage.onChanged either way.\n      await chrome.storage.session.set({ [ACTIVE_EID_KEY]: msg.eid });\n      return ok({ opened });\n    }"

## "Syncing with changes" — what's actually expected

In Option B, the panel reflects **saved** state. It does **not** live-update as you type/edit before saving — that's the add-on-only capability we deliberately dropped. So:
- **Opening a saved event → should load its roster** (one-time). ✅ expected to work.
- **Editing guests and seeing it update live** → not supported pre-save; the background poll refreshes it within ~1 min *after you save*. This is by design, not a bug.

So the real bug to chase is: **opening a saved event isn't loading it into the panel.**

## The prime suspect: the deployed engine doesn't accept the extension's token yet

This is almost certainly it. The extension talks to the **deployed** dev engine (`ops-engine-dev-330299…`). But my `audiences()` change (to read `AUXILIO_EXTENSION_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`) is **only in your local engine source — uncommitted and undeployed.** The deployed engine still reads **only** `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`. - Google sign-in succeeds (that's between you and Google),
- but the extension's `id_token` (audience `561888594292-…`) is **rejected by the engine with 401**, so `/addon/draft` fails and the panel shows nothing / bounces back to sign-in.

**Quickest fix to test right now (no deploy):** add the extension's client id to the **existing** `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` on the deployed engine as a comma-separated second value, and restart it:

Rebuilt with diagnostics. Now let's capture exactly what the Calendar API is rejecting.

1. **Reload the extension** (remove + Load unpacked from `.output/chrome-mv3`).
2. Open the **service worker** console: `chrome://extensions` → Auxilio Visitor → click **"service worker"** → Console tab. (The resolve runs in the background worker, not the panel — so this is the console that matters.)
3. Open an event → **Register a visitor**. Watch for these lines:
   - `[auxilio] resolve event { eid, eventId, calendarId }`
   - if it fails: `[auxilio] events.get failed 404 <body>` (and maybe a `→ retrying on primary` line)
4. **Paste those lines here.**

That tells us precisely:
- what `eventId` / `calendarId` we decoded from the chip, and
- the 404 body from Google (often says *why*).

My suspects, which the logs will confirm:
- **It's not a normal event** — e.g. a birthday, holiday, Tasks item, or an event from a *subscribed* calendar. Those chips carry `data-eventid`s that aren't fetchable via `events.get` → 404. Try clicking a **plain meeting you created** and see if that one resolves.
- **A calendar-id mismatch** the new `primary` fallback should now catch (you'll see the retry line).
- A recurring-instance id edge case.

To be clear on your "not communicating with our backend" instinct: you're right that it isn't reaching the engine **yet** — but that's because this Calendar-API resolve step fails first and short-circuits. Auth and Google comms are working. Once `events.get` returns the event, the very next call is to our engine (`/addon/draft`), and *then* the engine-audience thing I mentioned (adding the extension's client id to `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` on the deployed engine) becomes the next gate.

Paste the SW console lines and I'll pinpoint it.

> DEVELOPER

how is the extension fetching the calendar event of signed in user, directly or through our engine?

> AGENT

**Directly** — the extension fetches the event from the Google Calendar API itself, not through our engine.

There are two separate calls, with two separate tokens:

| Step | Who it talks to | Token | Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Resolve the event** (get iCalUID + attendees) | **Google Calendar API directly** (`https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/...events/{id}`) | `access_token` (Calendar read) | `lib/calendar.ts` → `fetchActiveEvent` (background worker) |
| **Register / draft** | **Our engine** (`/api/visitor/calendar/addon/*`) | `id_token` (Bearer) | `lib/engine.ts` |

So the flow is: extension → **Google** (fetch the event) → then extension → **our engine** (send the resolved event data to create the draft/passes). The engine does **not** fetch the event from Google for the extension; it receives the event data the extension already resolved (that's why we send `iCalUid` + `attendees` in the `/addon/draft` body).

**Why direct:** that's the "Calendar read scope" decision you picked at planning time — the extension holds `calendar.events.readonly`, so it reads the authoritative event client-side. The alternative (engine fetches it) would need the engine to hold *that user's* calendar OAuth, which most users don't have.

**What this means for your current error:** the `404 "event not found"` is on the **direct extension → Google** call. Our engine isn't in that path at all yet — which confirms your instinct that the engine isn't being hit, but the reason isn't a backend connectivity problem; it's that the Google `events.get` is failing before the engine call ever happens. So the fix is in the event-id/Calendar-API resolve (the logs I just added), not the backend.

Once `events.get` returns the event, the *next* hop is the engine — and that's where the `AUXILIO_WORKSPACE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` audience thing becomes the gate.

> AGENT

Two distinct findings, both useful:

**Unsaved event** (`Event not found`): that's actually *correct and unavoidable* — an unsaved event doesn't exist on Google's servers yet, so `events.get` legitimately 404s. The extension reflects saved state only (Option B), so there's genuinely nothing to fetch until you save. That just needs a friendlier message.

**Saved event** (title shows, rest stuck loading): this is the real signal. Once you see the **title + skeleton rows**, it means the Calendar resolve *succeeded* and the panel is now waiting on the **engine** `/addon/draft` call — which is hanging and never completing or erroring. That call is pending forever, so I need to give it a **timeout** and **surface the real error** instead of an infinite spinner. Let me do that.

JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,\n      signal: ctrl.signal,\n    });\n  } catch (err) {\n    if ((err as Error).name === 'AbortError') {\n      throw new EngineError(\n        `Engine did not respond within 20s (${url}). Is it reachable?`,\n        0,\n      );\n    }\n    throw new EngineError(\n      `Could not reach the engine (${(err as Error).message}). Check WXT_ENGINE_URL / host_permissions.`,\n      0,\n    );\n  } finally {\n    clearTimeout(timeout);\n  }\n  const text = await res.text();\n  console.log('[auxilio] engine ←', res.status, `${Date.now() - started}ms`, text.slice(0, 200));\n  let data: { error?: string } = {};\n  try {\n    data = text ? JSON.parse(text) : {};\n  } catch {\n    if (!res.ok) throw new EngineError(`Engine error ${res.status}: ${text.slice(0, 140)}`, res.status);\n  }\n  if (!res.ok) {\n    throw new EngineError(data?.error ?? `Request failed (${res.status})`, res.status);\n  }\n  return data as T;\n}"
}

Built clean. But thinking about your exact symptom — **"only the title, rest stuck loading forever"** — I think I've spotted the actual bug, separate from the engine hang.

The panel shows the title via the **roster skeleton** (which displays `event.title` + skeleton rows). That skeleton renders whenever the draft has no data. If the resolved event came back with an **empty `iCalUID`**, the draft query is **disabled** (it requires an iCalUid) — so it never fetches, never errors, and sits on the skeleton **forever**. That matches your symptom precisely. Let me guard against it and log the resolved event so we can confirm.

Built clean. **Reload the extension** and open a **saved** event → Register a visitor. The infinite skeleton is now impossible — you'll land on one of these, each of which tells us the cause:

1. **Roster loads** → it was the engine being slow; now it completes. 🎉
2. **"Can't register from this event — no calendar UID"** → the resolve returned an empty `iCalUID`. That's the bug, and the next fix is in how we read it.
3. **An engine error** (e.g. *"Engine did not respond within 20s"*, *"host domain not allowed"*, a 401/403/500 message) → now visible instead of hanging; tells us it's the backend/audience config.

Whichever it is, that on-screen message is the diagnosis.

**Most useful next step:** with the **service worker** console open (`chrome://extensions` → Auxilio Visitor → "service worker"), do it once and read these lines:
- `[auxilio] resolved event { iCalUID, summary, attendees }` — is `iCalUID` present or empty/undefined?
- `[auxilio] engine → POST …/draft` then `[auxilio] engine ← <status> <ms> <body>` — what status, how long, what body?

Paste those two and I'll know exactly which of the three it is and fix the root cause. My ranked bets: (a) engine returning 401/403 because the deployed engine's audience list doesn't include the extension's client id yet, or (b) empty `iCalUID` on resolve.

lets do one thing, instead of showing register visitor button on the calendar homescreen, lets just show the button on the calendar event modal or expanded screen(the screen where we see more option of calendar event). this way we can fetch more details of the exact calendar event the user is intended to create invite passes. probably information of even unsaved calendar event. do let me know if you have better suggestion

> AGENT

Before I build this, let me separate the two things you're hoping for, because one is a clear win and the other has an architectural catch worth knowing.

## The UX change: yes, good idea — with a nuance

Showing the button **contextually when an event's detail popover / expanded edit screen is open** (instead of a corner FAB that latches onto any clicked chip) is genuinely better: it's unambiguous about *which* event, and it appears exactly where you're looking. I'm on board with that part.

The nuance is **how** we place it:
- **Inject our button *into* Google's modal/edit toolbar** — looks most "native," but it means coupling to Google's obfuscated modal markup (finding the right container, surviving their UI changes). That's *more* DOM tax — the opposite of the Option B principle we just hardened around.
- **Our own button, gated to appear only when the event surface is open** (still our shadow-DOM button, but it shows only while a popover/edit screen is open and targets *that* event's `data-eventid`). Nearly the same UX, no injection into Google's DOM, stays robust.

## The catch: "more details / unsaved events" — this is a misconception worth correcting

Two things, and they're independent of where the button lives:

1. **For a *saved* event, we already fetch *everything* via the Calendar API** (all attendees, organizer, times) from the `data-eventid`. The expanded screen gives us **nothing extra** — button placement doesn't add detail.

2. **For an *unsaved* event, the data exists only in the edit-form DOM.** Reaching it means scraping Google's guest-chip inputs — the fragile pre-save path we deliberately excluded. And there's a deeper blocker: **the engine keys everything on `iCalUID`, which doesn't exist until the event is saved.** So even if we scraped the unsaved guests, we'd have no stable key to create a tracked pass — it'd be orphaned from the dedup/lifecycle the whole architecture relies on. If the user never saves, you've issued passes for a phantom event.

So **registering on a truly unsaved event isn't really viable** — not because of the button, but because there's no `iCalUID` to anchor it. The correct flow is: add guests → **Save** (now it has an `iCalUID`) → register. Our "save first" message already nudges exactly that, and the sync-poll already fires the badge/notification the moment such an event is saved.

## My recommendation

Make the button **contextual to the open event surface (popover + expanded edit)** — your core instinct — using our **own gated button**, not injection, to keep it robust. Keep the "save first" guard for the pre-save case rather than chasing unsaved data. That gives you the cleaner targeting you want without the fragility or the orphaned-pass problem.

One decision is genuinely yours, since it changes robustness vs. native-feel:

Answering first, because this decides how the "Manage Visitors" gate should work.

## Can we read event data in realtime from the Calendar?

Split it into two cases — they have very different answers:

### Case 1 — a **saved** event → YES, we already can (all of it)
The Calendar API gives us the full event from the `data-eventid`. We currently fetch name, guests, time, and location; **rooms** are just attendees with `resource: true` (we fetch them, we're filtering them out), and **description** we can add to the field mask in one line. So for a saved event we can get **name, guests, time, location, rooms, description — authoritatively and robustly, no DOM scraping.** Nothing is blocked here; if you're missing description/rooms it's only because I haven't included them yet.

This isn't "realtime as you type," but for a saved event it's complete and always correct.

### Case 2 — **live / pre-save** (as you're typing in the open event, before saving) → only via the DOM
That in-progress data exists **only in the page's DOM** (the popover/edit form). We *can* read it — the title input, guest chips, time pickers, location, rooms, description are all sitting there, so technically yes, we can pull every field live. **But** that's exactly the DOM-scraping we deliberately walled off in Option B:
- It couples us to Google's obfuscated markup (breaks when they reshuffle it) — the maintenance tax.
- A pre-save event has **no `iCalUID`**, so the engine has no stable key to attach passes to — register-before-save is architecturally broken regardless of whether we can read the fields.

So: **the data is readable live, but it's the fragile path, and pre-save registration doesn't have a sound anchor.**

## What this means for your "Manage Visitors" gate

To show the button **only when the magic address is in the guest list**, you need to know the guest list at button-decision time. Two ways:

- **Light DOM scan (recommended for the gate):** when an event surface is open, scan its visible text/guest chips for `WXT_MAGIC_ADDRESS`. This is a **small, contained** read — same risk class as `data-eventid` — and it works in realtime, including while editing. It only decides *whether to show the button*; authoritative data still comes from the API when you open the panel.
- **API check:** call the API on every popover to read attendees, then decide. Only works for saved events, adds a round-trip + latency before the button can appear, and spams the API. Worse.

So my recommendation: use the **light DOM scan of the open event for the magic address** to gate the "Manage Visitors" button (realtime, contained), and keep the **API as the authoritative source** for the actual managing. I'd also add **description + rooms** to the API fetch so the panel shows them.

That's a *small, deliberate* widening of the DOM dependency (from "data-eventid + dialog-open" to "+ scan open-event text for one string") — still nowhere near full pre-save mirroring.

Want me to proceed on that basis — rename to **Manage Visitors**, gate it on the magic address via the light DOM scan, and add description/rooms to the API fetch? Or keep the gate API-only (saved events only)?

**The layering:**
- **DOM layer (content script):** instant + realtime + works pre-save. Used to (a) **gate** the button — scan the open event for the magic address, (b) provide an **instant snapshot** (guest emails) so the panel paints immediately, (c) cover the **pre-save** case where the API has nothing.
- **API layer (background):** authoritative + reliable. The source of truth for managing/sending (name, guests, time, location, **rooms**, **description**), and the only path that yields an `iCalUID` for actually issuing passes.
- **Merge rule:** panel shows the DOM snapshot instantly → reconciles to API data when it arrives → if the event is unsaved (API 404), it keeps the DOM data as a read-only preview with "save to issue passes."
